evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-bigger-choice

把输入框右下角那个**内置模型选择器**的下拉框做大做清楚：一屏能直接看到十几个模型，并且随时看得出「这批模型属于哪个提供商」。

纯客户端插件：只往页面里注入一份样式表，不动任何逻辑、不接管任何插槽。装完即生效（刷新页面后）。

## 它改了什么

内置下拉框由 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-model-selection` 渲染，宿主对它的尺寸写死了上限：

| | 原生 | 本插件 |
|---|---|---|
| `max-height` | `min(360px, 100vh - 96px)` | `min(78vh, 100vh - 24px)` |
| `width` | `max-content`（跟着内容） | `max-content`（重申，别被拉走） |
| `min-width` | `min(240px, 100vw - 32px)` | `min(240px, 100vw - 24px)`（保留原下限） |
| `max-width` | `min(420px, 100vw - 32px)` | `min(720px, 100vw - 24px)` |

行高（34px）不动，所以 756px 高的窗口里可见行数从约 10 行涨到约 15–16 行；窗口越高看到越多。

**宽度是自适应的**：宿主本来就给弹层 `width: max-content`——最长的一行（模型名或提供商名 + 末尾的打勾）有多宽，弹层就有多宽。第一版把它连同 `min-width` 一起撑到 360px，于是每行都空出一道「名字 → 打勾」的空白。现在 `min-width` 退回 240px 这个原下限，宽度重新由内容决定；`max-width` 只兜住超长名字，不让弹层拉穿视口。

> 已知边界：列表长到需要滚动时，竖直滚动条会吃掉内容区约 8px 宽，**最长的那个名字**可能因此被省略号截掉一两个字符。这是「宽度跟随内容」与「滚动条占位」的固有矛盾（滚动条不参与 `max-content` 计算），代价最小的一侧就是放过最长那一行。

## 提供商名（分组标题）

「CodeArts Agent」「CodeBuddy（腾讯）」这类行是 `MenuGroup` 渲染的 sticky 标题，
宿主样式是 **11px / `label-tertiary` 灰字 / 透明底**，只有真正吸顶那一刻才铺一层底色——
所以平时几乎看不见，也就分不清某个模型属于谁。本插件把它改成一条常驻色带：

| | 原生 | 本插件 |
|---|---|---|
| 字号 / 字重 | 11px / 500 | 12px / 600 |
| 颜色 | `--dsw-alias-label-tertiary` | `--dsw-alias-label-primary` |
| 背景 | 透明（仅吸顶时铺色） | 常驻 `--dsw-alias-menu-group-header-fill` |
| 内边距 | `4px 7px 2px` | `8px 8px 5px` |
| 组间距 | `3px` | `8px` |
| 下沿 | 无 | 1px `--dsw-alias-border-l2` |

关键是**常驻**：色带一直钉在列表顶部，所以「眼下这批模型属于哪个提供商」永远看得见，
不用往回滚去找那一行。吸顶时不再变色，也就没有滚动闪烁。

选择器在这里**不用 hash**——`MenuGroup` 会给标题打 `data-menu-group-heading`，
宿主自己的 `observeStickyMenuGroups()` 就是靠这个属性找分组的，属于它自己的契约面，
升级不会变。外面仍然限定在模型选择器的弹层里（用滚动容器的 `id$="-models"` 收窄），
不会波及别处恰好也用 MenuGroup 的菜单。

## 为什么改样式表就够了

弹层是 React portal（`position: fixed`），但**位置和尺寸都是宿主自己算的**：弹出前先
`menuRef.current.offsetHeight` 量一次，再把 `top` 夹进视口（`MARGIN = 12`），并在
`scroll` / `resize` 时重算。我们的样式表在插件加载时就已生效，所以宿主第一次量到的
就是放大后的高度，它会自己把菜单摆正——不会顶出屏幕，也不需要我们碰 `top/left`。

## 弹层的选择器

```css
._7KE1Ra_menu,
[id$="-menu"][class*="_menu"]:has([class*="_groups"]) { … }
```

* `._7KE1Ra_menu`：本机这一版 DSH 构建出的 CSS-module 类名（hash 由源码内容决定）。
* 第二条是 **DSH 升级后的兜底**：hash 变了也没关系——宿主给弹层的 id 是自己拼的
  `id={id}-menu`，而 `_menu` / `_groups` 是该模块**本地**的类名（本地类名不变则后缀不变）；
  再要求弹层里真的装着那个滚动容器，避开其它恰好叫 `*_menu` 的弹层。

两条都靠 CSS-module 的 `<hash>_<localName>` 命名约定，不改任何宿主代码。

## 想再调大/调小、想换标题色

五个旋钮都走 CSS 自定义属性，devtools 或你自己的样式表里覆盖即可，不用重装：

```css
:root {
  /* 弹层尺寸 */
  --dsh-bigger-choice-max-height: min(90vh, 100vh - 16px);
  --dsh-bigger-choice-min-width: min(320px, 100vw - 24px);
  --dsh-bigger-choice-max-width: min(760px, 100vw - 24px);
  /* 提供商标题栏 */
  --dsh-bigger-choice-group-color: var(--dsw-alias-label-secondary);
  --dsh-bigger-choice-group-size: 13px;
}
```

想让每行都空出固定宽度（例如把「名字 → 打勾」那块拉开），把 `min-width` 调大即可——
宽度本来跟着内容走，`min-width` 一抬高就成了一条固定的下限。

## 结构

| 文件 | 作用 |
|---|---|
| `package.json` | bundle 元数据（`dsh.bundle.patch` + `dsh.client`） |
| `cordis.patch.yml` | 插入一行 `dsh-bigger-choice` |
| `index.js` | 宿主半身，空实现（本插件不需要宿主服务） |
| `client.js` | 客户端半身：注入 `/1` 中的那份样式表 |
| `icon.svg` | 图标 |

## 已知边界

* 这是**刻意覆盖宿主弹层**，不是官方插槽能力：`_7KE1Ra_menu` 这个 hash 会随 DSH 升级变化，
  届时靠第二条选择器继续命中；若某次升级连 `_menu` / `_groups` 的本地类名也改了，需要重新对一次。
* 只放大「模型选择器」这一个弹层。宽度是自适应的（跟随最长一行），模型名不会换行。
* 提供商色带是**常驻**的：宿主原本只在吸顶时铺底色，这里改成一直铺。如果你更想要宿主的
  原行为（只在吸顶时铺色），把那一行的背景换成透明即可。

## 验证到什么程度

* 宿主侧：`cordis.yml` 里已落行（`- id: dsh-bigger-choice` / `name: dsh-bigger-choice`），
  运行中的 Loader 也能查到这条 entry（`include:dsh-bigger-choice`，`status: absent`＝无 Config，正常）。
* 客户端半身：用 DOM 桩子真跑了一遍 `client.js`（注册 → factory → `apply(ctx)`），**42 项断言全过**——
  含「脚本执行期不碰 DOM」「`apply` 只挂一份 `<style>`」「重复 `apply` 不叠加」「没有 `ctx.effect` 也能生效」、
  样式表的花括号配平、**每个 `var()` 引用的自定义属性都有定义**（防 token 名写错），
  以及四个盒模型属性、宽度确实走 `max-content`、`min-width` 没有被人为提高、
  提供商色带的两条选择器与取值确实写对了。
* 没做：真实浏览器里的视觉截图。这一步需要带 token 的页面（无头访问 `/` 得到 401），
  所以「刷新后肉眼看到框变大 / 变宽」由使用者确认。

# @agentrq/dsh-plugin-agentrq

AgentRQ task manager for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness).

Create, manage, and automatically receive [AgentRQ](https://agentrq.com) tasks without leaving the harness. The bundle ships two rows: the workspace's tools bridged to the model, and the harness-side behavior a tool bridge cannot provide on its own — a supervised workspace session that opens a dedicated dsh session for each task AgentRQ pushes, and the AgentRQ working agreement as a system-prompt section.

## Install

**Requires pnpm.** `dsh plugin` is a thin forwarder to `pnpm` for every profile — installing any plugin, this one included, fails with `pnpm not found on PATH` unless pnpm is already installed (`npm install -g pnpm`, `corepack enable pnpm`, or `brew install pnpm`). This is a DeepSeek Harness CLI requirement, not something this plugin can opt out of.

**One profile per workspace.** A profile serves one AgentRQ workspace and carries its own endpoint, so name it after the workspace rather than using `default` — that is what makes [several workspaces](#multiple-workspaces) work. Your workspace's **Settings → Setup → DeepSeek Harness** page prints every command and config block below already filled in.

```sh
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile agentrq-<workspace> add @agentrq/dsh-plugin-agentrq
```

Then pin this workspace's endpoint in the profile's own patch layer, `~/.dsh/profiles/agentrq-<workspace>/cordis.patch.yml`. Copy the URL from the Settings page — it already carries the `?token=` credential that authenticates a headless client:

```yaml
- id: agentrq
  name: '@agentrq/dsh-plugin-agentrq'
  config:
    url: "https://<workspace>.mcp.agentrq.com/mcp?token=<token>"
```

One row, one URL: the plugin mounts `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` itself as a child fiber, so the endpoint is configured in exactly one place and the bridge shares this row's lifetime — disposal and HMR take it along.

```sh
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh --profile agentrq-<workspace> --dump-config   # shows the bundle layer and your override
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh --profile agentrq-<workspace>
```

The profile's patch is applied after every bundle layer, so those two rows win. dsh watches both `cordis.patch.yml` layers and reapplies valid edits transactionally, so changing the URL takes effect without a restart.

### Using dsh web (browser UI)

`dsh web` is an alias for `--profile web` — a fixed, dsh-shipped profile that is a different profile from any `agentrq-<workspace>` profile made above, and the two do not share bundles. Installing into one does not make the plugin visible in the other. To use this plugin from the harness's browser UI, target `web` directly:

```sh
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile web add @agentrq/dsh-plugin-agentrq
```

Then either pin the endpoint in `~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml` (same block as above) or export `AGENTRQ_WORKSPACE_MCP_URL` before starting:

```sh
export AGENTRQ_WORKSPACE_MCP_URL='https://<workspace>.mcp.agentrq.com/mcp?token=<token>'
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web
```

Because [a single profile cannot serve two workspaces](#multiple-workspaces), only one AgentRQ workspace can be wired into the browser UI this way — use the `--profile agentrq-<workspace>` flow above for several at once.

### Configuring without a file edit

The bundle's own patch defaults both rows to `!!js process.env.AGENTRQ_WORKSPACE_MCP_URL`, so a container or CI job can export the endpoint instead of writing a profile patch:

```sh
export AGENTRQ_WORKSPACE_MCP_URL='https://<workspace>.mcp.agentrq.com/mcp?token=<token>'
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh --profile agentrq-<workspace>
```

Prefer the profile patch for an interactive install: an environment variable is process-global, so with one profile per workspace you have to remember the right `export` before each start, and the wrong one connects the wrong workspace without complaint. Supply neither and the row fails to load with the `url` field named — it is a required field, not a silent default.

Installing from a git checkout instead of the registry fetches sources rather than built artifacts, so pnpm must be allowed to run this package's `prepare` build. Add the allowance to your profile's `pnpm-workspace.yaml` and re-run the `add`:

```yaml
allowBuilds:
  '@agentrq/dsh-plugin-agentrq': true
```

That allowance is permission to execute this package's code on your machine at install time. Pin a commit (`github:agentrq/agentrq#<sha>`) if you take that route. Publishing to npm or shipping a `pnpm pack` tarball avoids the allowance entirely.

## What the model gets

Every tool the workspace server offers — seven today, each taking an `action` and its `payload` — bridged by `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` under the `agentrq` namespace:

| Tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `mcp__agentrq__task` | The workspace's tasks: `get` (with no `taskId`, dequeue the next one assigned to this agent), `create`, `updateStatus` (`ongoing`, `completed`, `blocked`, …), `reply` — the only thing the remote human sees — `elicit` (ask and wait for the answer) and `getAttachment` |
| `mcp__agentrq__memory` | What the workspace remembers: `load` (with no name, `memory.md`, the index), `save` (replaces a memory entirely), `delete` |
| `mcp__agentrq__skills` | The workspace's skills: `search` (by name or description, with their `skill://` URIs), `load`, `save`, `delete` |
| `mcp__agentrq__workspace` | `get` (the workspace title and mission) and `publishEvent` (fire a named event so subscriber workspaces spawn their trigger tasks) |
| `mcp__agentrq__siteTools` | Websites the human shared from the Chrome extension: `search` their WebMCP tools (`q` for BM25, `pattern` for a regex, `limit`/`offset` to page), `getDefinition` (input schema, before calling), `call` (in the human's Chrome; a tool not marked read-only asks the human first) |
| `mcp__agentrq__pano` | Markdown docs every workspace of the account shares: `save`, `read`, `comment`, `attach`, `delete` |
| `mcp__agentrq__help` | How to call the others: every tool, one tool's actions, or one action's payload with an example (`{"action": "task.create"}`) |

Plus one tool this package owns:

| Tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `agentrq_autopull` | `status`, `pause`, `resume`, or `pull_now` for this session's AgentRQ delivery |

`pull_now` returns the dequeued task as its own tool result rather than queuing a turn, because a tool body runs mid-turn by definition.

## How work arrives

**The plugin does not poll.** AgentRQ already decides when there is work and pushes it over `notifications/claude/channel`:

- creating a task assigned to the agent pushes it immediately (`backend/internal/handler/api/task.go`), provided nothing else is ongoing;
- `WorkspaceServer.StartPoller` re-pushes the next unclaimed task — or a status check for the ongoing one — every 60 seconds.

The plugin's own workspace session subscribes to that channel, exactly as [`acp-gateway`](https://github.com/agentrq/agentrq-acp-gateway) does for Gemini and other ACP agents. Polling the queue from the client would duplicate the server's own ticker and deliver every task twice.

Each push is forwarded **as written**. A new task, the periodic reminder, a status check, and a human's reply all arrive on the same channel; the plugin adds a framing line naming the `chat_id` and the tools to answer with, then hands over the content. It does not try to classify what kind of push it is, because that would only add a way to be wrong. The content is JSON-escaped into the framing, so pushed content cannot forge a framing field.

**Each task gets its own dedicated dsh session.** The plugin's own workspace connection is not tied to any chat you open — the first push for a given task (its `chat_id`) opens a fresh, dedicated agent via `ctx.agents.create()` and hands it the framed push; every later push for that same task (the reminder, a status check, a human's reply) is routed into that same session, not into whatever chat you happen to have open. This is what keeps one task's history from bleeding into another's. Delivery route within a task's session depends on its agent's state: `inject()` while a turn is running, so it lands at the next step boundary, and `followup()` while idle, since nothing else would wake it. Neither interrupts a turn in flight.

A session created with no provider/model fails every turn outright (prompt assembly has no value for `{{model}}`), and one created with the wrong `cwd` leaves the agent unable to find its own codebase, groups as "Ungrouped" instead of under your project in a capable UI, and can fall back to naming the session after that wrong directory (prompt assembly also has no value for `{{cwd}}` with none set at all). So every dedicated session gets an explicit `cwd` and `agentOptions`: `cwd`/`provider`/`model` config when set, otherwise both come from the *reference agent* — whichever live agent in the same process most recently started a turn (tracked from `agent/status` since the manager started), falling back to the longest-lived agent still around when nothing has been active yet. **`cwd` deliberately does not fall back to `process.cwd()`** except as an absolute last resort (no reference agent at all): under `dsh web`, the harness process's own cwd is the dsh *profile* directory (e.g. `~/.dsh/profiles/web`), not the project a human actually works in, and defaulting to it left a real dedicated session stuck for dozens of steps trying to locate a codebase that was never there. There is no way to ask the harness for its own configured default model/cwd from a plugin, only to read them off an agent that already has them, so the very first task pushed before this process has ever seen any activity still fails/misbehaves unless `model` (and, if the process cwd is wrong for this deployment, `cwd`) is configured explicitly.

`SendChannelNotification` puts the task id in `meta.chat_id` on every push, so the id never has to be recovered from the content, and it doubles as the key the manager uses to find a task's session again.

**A newly opened session is titled and grouped, not left for a UI to guess at.** A session's display name is a durable `session/title` log event (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-title`) — never inferred from a message's content, and even that package's own deterministic fallback only considers genuinely human-sourced messages, which this plugin's pushes never are. So the manager calls `sessionTitle.rename(session, title)` directly: the task's own title when the push already carries it (the startup catch-up path), otherwise fetched via `task` `get` — one extra round trip, only the first time a task's session opens, skipped silently (with a warning) if the lookup fails or the task has no title. Grouping works the same way: a session is never folded into a workspace just because its `cwd` happens to match one (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-workspace`'s own docs: "later cwd-only sessions remain Ungrouped") — the manager resolves or creates the workspace owning the session's `cwd` and calls `Workspace.attachSession` explicitly. Both `sessionTitle` and `workspaceRegistry` are optional host services (`ctx.get(name)`, never a direct `ctx.sessionTitle`/`ctx.workspaceRegistry` read — that assumes an `inject`-declared, guaranteed-present service, which these deliberately aren't); a deployment without session persistence mounts neither, and the session still works, just untitled and ungrouped.

**A task's session survives a harness restart.** The manager's live task→session map is only ever in memory, but a session's own id already encodes its task id (`agentrq-task-<taskId>-<random>`), so nothing separate needs to persist it: at startup the manager lists every session `@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-persistence` already knows about (headers only, not full logs), and the first push for a task whose session survived resumes it (`ctx.agents.resume`) instead of opening a duplicate. A resume that fails (a corrupted log, say) falls back to opening fresh rather than blocking delivery. The random suffix matters here, not just for looks: an incrementing in-process counter resets across a restart, and the moment the same task got pushed twice across one, the persistence layer rejected the reused id outright as already belonging to a different session.

**Repeats are dropped.** The workspace re-pushes an unclaimed task verbatim every minute; the manager remembers recent `(task, content)` pairs, so a task's session is handed it once and not woken every sixty seconds for work it already has. A genuinely new message on the same task still gets through.

**A task's session closes itself once the task is done.** An idle agent does not by itself mean the task is finished — it may simply have asked the human a question and be waiting on a reply, which must land in the same session. So on every idle transition the manager reads the task's own status back through `task` `get`; only `completed` or `rejected` closes the dedicated session. `blocked` and anything else keep it open so the next push — including the human's reply — still has somewhere to go.

**Staying connected is the load-bearing part.** No workspace session, no pushes — so a closed transport or an unrecoverable transport error triggers a reconnect with exponential backoff (`reconnect.initialDelayMs` doubling to `reconnect.maxDelayMs`), on top of the SDK's own SSE resumption. Because the server re-pushes on its own schedule, a recovered connection catches up on the next tick without any client-side replay. A task's own dedicated session is unaffected by a workspace reconnect — it is a separate, harness-native agent, not part of the workspace transport.

`catchUpOnStart` dequeues one task when the workspace connection opens, so work that predates the connection does not wait for the server's next tick. A failed startup check costs latency, not work.

`agentrq_autopull pause` stops the manager from opening or routing into task sessions; already-open ones stay live until their task closes them, and the workspace connection itself stays open.

## Multiple workspaces

AgentRQ users normally have several workspaces, each with its own queue, mission, and agent identity. **Run one profile per workspace.**

Install once per profile, and let each profile's `cordis.patch.yml` carry its own endpoint:

```sh
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile agentrq-acme add @agentrq/dsh-plugin-agentrq
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile agentrq-beta add @agentrq/dsh-plugin-agentrq
# …then pin acme's URL in ~/.dsh/profiles/agentrq-acme/cordis.patch.yml
#     and beta's URL in ~/.dsh/profiles/agentrq-beta/cordis.patch.yml

npx @deepseek-ai/dsh --profile agentrq-acme    # terminal 1
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh --profile agentrq-beta    # terminal 2
```

Because the endpoint lives in the profile rather than the environment, switching workspaces is switching profiles — nothing to re-export, and no way to start one workspace's profile pointed at another's queue.

Each profile gets its own process, sessions, working directory, and workspace connection, which matches how AgentRQ already models a workspace: one workspace, one agent, one mission. It also matches the usual case where workspaces track different repositories.

Two consequences worth knowing:

- **A single profile cannot serve two workspaces.** Mounting the bundle twice in one profile registers the `agentrq:protocol` prompt section and the `agentrq_autopull` tool twice in the same layer, and both registrations throw on a duplicate name. Namespacing them per instance is deferred until someone needs it.
- **No cross-workspace view.** AgentRQ's CoreMCP supervisor (`https://mcp.agentrq.com/mcp`) does expose `workspace.list` and `task.listAll`, so a deployment that wants "what is outstanding everywhere" can mount it as an extra `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` row. It sends no channel notifications, so it complements per-workspace delivery rather than replacing it.

`serverName` is safe to change: the guidance section and every framing derive their tool names from it, so the namespace the model sees and the namespace the prose describes cannot drift apart.

## Config

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `url` | — (required) | Workspace MCP endpoint, including its `?token=` credential |
| `token` | `''` | Bearer token, for deployments that prefer an `Authorization` header over `?token=` |
| `mountBridge` | `true` | Mount the `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` child that gives the model AgentRQ's tools |
| `serverName` | `agentrq` | Namespace for the bridged tools; the guidance section and framings follow it |
| `deliverPushes` | `true` | Open and route into a dedicated session for each task the workspace pushes |
| `catchUpOnStart` | `true` | Dequeue one task when the workspace connection opens |
| `reconnect.initialDelayMs` | `1000` | Delay before the first reconnect attempt |
| `reconnect.maxDelayMs` | `900000` | Ceiling for the reconnect backoff |
| `guidance` | `true` | Contribute the AgentRQ working-agreement system-prompt section |
| `requestTimeoutMs` | `30000` | Timeout for one AgentRQ tool call |
| `provider` | `''` | Provider route for each task's dedicated session. Empty copies the most recently active agent's provider |
| `model` | `''` | Model id for each task's dedicated session. Empty copies the most recently active agent's model |
| `cwd` | `''` | Working directory for each task's dedicated session. Empty copies the reference agent's cwd (see above) — **not** the dsh process's own cwd, which under `dsh web` is the profile directory, not your project |

Set any of these in the same profile patch. A patch replaces a row's whole `config` rather than merging into it, but every key except `url` has a schema default, so a row only restates what it changes:

```yaml
- id: agentrq
  name: '@agentrq/dsh-plugin-agentrq'
  config:
    url: "https://<workspace>.mcp.agentrq.com/mcp?token=<token>"
    catchUpOnStart: false
    reconnect:
      initialDelayMs: 2000
      maxDelayMs: 60000
```

## The prompt section

AgentRQ's MCP server ships its collaboration rules as server `Instructions`, and the harness does not surface an MCP server's instructions to the model. Without them the model has the tools but not the contract — that the human is remote, sees only what `task` `reply` sends, and needs the task claimed before work starts. This package contributes those rules as the `agentrq:protocol` section in the tool-guidance band (order 150), so behavior in dsh matches behavior in the Claude Code and Gemini extensions. Turn it off with `guidance: false` when a deployment states the same protocol in its own persona.

## Development

```sh
npm install --legacy-peer-deps   # harness packages declare peers pnpm resolves from the profile
npm run typecheck
npm test
npm run build
```

`make plugin-deepseek` from the repository root runs all four.

## Releasing

`.github/workflows/plugin-deepseek-harness.yml` typechecks, tests, and builds this package on every pull request that touches `plugins/deepseek-harness/**`, and publishes it to npm when such a change lands on `main`.

**Bumping `version` in `package.json` is what releases.** npm refuses to republish an existing version, so the workflow checks first and skips the publish when the current version is already on the registry — an ordinary fix that touches this path does not need a version bump to merge.

Authentication is [npm trusted publishing](https://docs.npmjs.com/trusted-publishers): the package names `agentrq/agentrq` and this workflow file as its trusted publisher, the job requests an OIDC token with `id-token: write`, and npm exchanges it for a short-lived publish credential. There is no `NPM_TOKEN` secret to store, rotate, or leak, and npm attaches build provenance automatically.

Two things that break it, both non-obvious:

- **Renaming the workflow file.** The trusted-publisher record names `plugin-deepseek-harness.yml` exactly; a rename must be made on npm's side too or every publish is rejected.
- **npm older than 11.5.1.** It has no OIDC support and silently falls back to looking for a token. The workflow installs npm 12.2.0 explicitly rather than trusting the one `setup-node` ships — do not remove that step.

## Known limitations and deferred work

- **Two pushes racing for the same brand-new task can still open two sessions** — `deliverPush` doesn't await the previous call for a different chat, so if two pushes for a task neither has seen before arrive close enough together, both can find no live *or* persisted session and both create one. Existing pushes for an already-open task don't have this problem (they queue into the resolved session, live or resumed).
- **One workspace per profile** — each row carries one `url`, and mounting the bundle twice in one profile collides on the prompt-section and tool names. [Several workspaces means several profiles](#multiple-workspaces).
- **The endpoint is configured, not discovered** — there is no in-harness command to switch workspaces; the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` (watched, so no restart needed) or `AGENTRQ_WORKSPACE_MCP_URL` is the switch. A `ctx.settings` namespace would give a schema-driven editor with `role('secret')` redaction for the token, but its document is `$DSH_HOME`-global by default and so does not carry per-profile values without extra plumbing.
- **The bridge is mounted, not injectable** — the plugin mounts one `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` child with the settings it derives from its own config. A deployment that needs the bridge's other knobs sets `mountBridge: false` and mounts its own row, and is then responsible for keeping `serverName` aligned.
- **No in-harness command lists or switches to a task's session** — it's titled and grouped correctly now (a capable UI like `dsh web` shows it in the sidebar under its project, named after the task), but there's still no dedicated "show me AgentRQ's sessions" affordance; you find one the way you'd find any other session there.
- **The very first task session can still fail if nothing else is configured** — `provider`/`model` default to copying the most recently active agent in the process, falling back to the longest-lived one if none has been active yet; if a task is pushed before any session has ever existed at all (e.g. right at process startup with `catchUpOnStart`), there is nothing to copy and the session opens with no model, which fails every turn. Set `model` (and `provider`, if it's not the deployment's default route) explicitly to avoid depending on load order.
- **Terminal-status check costs a round trip per idle transition** — the manager cannot tell "done" from "idle mid-task, waiting on a reply" without asking the workspace, so every `agent/status: idle` for a task's session calls `task` `get` once. Cheap in practice (one call per turn boundary, not per second), but not free.
- **Session-lifetime repeat memory** — the delivered-set is process-local and bounded, so a restarted harness may be handed a task it saw before if that task is still unclaimed. Claiming a task with `task` `updateStatus` is what stops the workspace re-pushing it.
- **Auth is the URL's credential** — the plugin does not run the AgentRQ OAuth authorization-code flow; it uses the long-lived token from Workspace Settings, as a bearer header or a `?token=` query parameter.
- **Attachments travel through the model** — the plugin's own session only receives pushes and dequeues on request; `getAttachment` remains a model-facing tool call on the bridged server.
- **Permission verdicts are not bridged** — `acp-gateway` also consumes `notifications/claude/channel/permission` to answer AgentRQ's allow/deny prompts. The harness has its own `tools/pre-execute` approval axis, and wiring the two together is deferred.

## License

[Apache-2.0](./LICENSE). The AgentRQ server itself is AGPL-3.0-only; this plugin, like the other published packages, keeps Apache-2.0.

# AgentRQ ── Agent-Human Collaboration Platform

<p align="center">
  <a href="README.zh-CN.md">简体中文</a>
  <br />
  <br />
  <a href="https://discord.gg/xFSMaEA2b2">
    <img src="https://img.shields.io/badge/Discord-Join%20Community-5865F2?style=for-the-badge&logo=discord&logoColor=white" alt="Discord" />

  <a href="https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/agentrq/iadkenmjgjoilnioldgchgjpdnbaghbj">
    <img src="https://img.shields.io/badge/Chrome%20Web%20Store-Add%20to%20Chrome-4285F4?style=for-the-badge&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white" alt="Chrome Web Store" />
  </a>
</p>

AgentRQ is a modern, high-performance platform designed for seamless collaboration between human operators and AI agents. It leverages the **Model Context Protocol (MCP)** to allow AI models (like Claude) to interact directly with your workspace's task management system.

## 🚀 Overview

Think of AgentRQ as a shared workspace where humans and AI agents work together seamlessly. You can break down complex goals into manageable tasks, and delegate work directly to your AI agents. 

Because agents "see" the workspace state via MCP, they can autonomously pull their assigned tasks, update statuses, request permissions for sensitive actions, and communicate with you—all synchronized instantly across the platform in real-time.

## ✨ Features

Real captures from the running app — no mockups.

<table>
<tr>
<td width="50%" valign="middle">

### Visual Task Board

Every task Claude creates appears instantly on your board. See what it's working on, what it needs, and what it just finished — all from a clean, fast dashboard you can open on any device, as a list or a Kanban.

</td>
<td width="50%"><img src="https://agentrq.com/assets/feature-task-board.gif" alt="AgentRQ active tasks dashboard and kanban board" width="320" /></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td width="50%"><img src="https://agentrq.com/assets/feature-task-scheduling.gif" alt="AgentRQ scheduled task auto-spawning into the dashboard" width="320" /></td>
<td width="50%" valign="middle">

### Task Scheduling

Give any task a launch date, or a recurring cadence — every 15 minutes, hourly, daily, weekly, custom days. A background poller ticks every minute and spawns the task the instant it's due, no server or agent needing to stay awake and wait.

</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td width="50%" valign="middle">

### Events

Events are named signals — `qa_passed`, `deploy_finished`, `blog_published` — that any task can fire when it completes. Wire one to a workspace and that workspace gets a new task automatically, no polling and no glue code.

</td>
<td width="50%"><img src="https://agentrq.com/assets/feature-events.gif" alt="AgentRQ events list and configured trigger" width="320" /></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td width="50%"><img src="https://agentrq.com/assets/feature-workflows.gif" alt="AgentRQ workflow node graph" width="320" /></td>
<td width="50%" valign="middle">

### Workflows

A Workflow is Events and workspaces arranged on a graph. Drag a workspace onto an event to subscribe it; drag an event onto a workspace to emit it on completion. No decision-tree DSL, no YAML — just the shape of your release process, visible.

</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td width="50%" valign="middle">

### Tool Call History

The task detail view's History tab lays out a lane-grouped timeline of every tool call and message in a run — Input, Agent, and Tools. Search it, click into any entry, and see exactly what ran, what it returned, and whether it was allowed or denied.

</td>
<td width="50%"><img src="https://agentrq.com/assets/feature-tool-call-history.gif" alt="AgentRQ tool call history trajectory panel" width="320" /></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td width="50%"><img src="https://agentrq.com/assets/feature-auto-title.gif" alt="AgentRQ auto-title generation in action" width="320" /></td>
<td width="50%" valign="middle">

### Auto-Title Generation

Write your task description, click the sparkle, and a small language model — downloaded once and cached by your browser — reads it and writes the title. No API call, no server, no data leaving your machine.

</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td width="50%" valign="middle">

### Speech-to-Text

Click the mic on any task description or reply and dictate it instead. Transcription runs on an in-browser Whisper model — your voice is processed on-device and never uploaded anywhere.

</td>
<td width="50%"><img src="https://agentrq.com/assets/feature-speech-to-text.gif" alt="AgentRQ speech-to-text mic entry point" width="320" /></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td width="50%"><img src="https://agentrq.com/assets/feature-message-send-delay.gif" alt="AgentRQ message send delay countdown with Send Now and Cancel" width="320" /></td>
<td width="50%" valign="middle">

### Message Send Delay

Give a workspace a countdown — 3s, 5s, 10s, 15s, 30s or 60s — and every chat message waits that long in the thread before it reaches the agent. **Send Now** delivers it early, **Cancel** pulls it back unsent and puts the exact text and attachments back in your composer. Off by default, per workspace.

</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td width="50%" valign="middle">

### Search & Keyboard Shortcuts

<kbd>⌘K</kbd> (<kbd>Ctrl+K</kbd> off macOS) opens a task finder that matches any word in a title or description, straight from the copy your device already saved — so it answers offline, and tells you how far it looked. Everything else is a bare letter: <kbd>N</kbd> for a new task, <kbd>W</kbd> and <kbd>M</kbd> to jump to a workspace or a machine, <kbd>P</kbd> for the Pano, <kbd>C</kbd> and <kbd>T</kbd> to flip between a task's chat and its trajectory, <kbd>?</kbd> for the list. Nothing to configure, and nothing to memorise.

</td>

# dsh-memory

![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@fooxe/dsh-memory) ![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue) ![node](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%3E%3D22.19-green)

**English** | [**中文版**](#中文版)

## English

**Persistent memory for DeepSeek Harness — the Claude Code memory model: your agents remember across sessions, wake up with context, and never mix projects. Pure files, zero dependencies.**

## What it does

> Your DSH agent meets you for the "first time" — **every single session**.
> With dsh-memory, it remembers.

```text
Session 1   You: "Remember — this project uses pnpm, not npm."
            Agent: saved via memory_save

Session 2   You: "Which package manager do we use?"
            Agent: "pnpm — you told me yesterday."   <- no re-asking, ever
```

No server, no account, no embedding provider. Just plain markdown files — delete the directory and that scope forgets everything.

## Highlights

### 🖥️ A visual memory manager, not a markdown dump

**Settings → Memory** opens a full manager: every memory from both scopes in one searchable list, workspaces as an expandable tree (nested sub-project scopes discovered automatically), sub-folder grouping, and live guard gauges (index lines / KB / file count). Add, rewrite, tag, or delete any memory **right in the panel** — through the exact same guarded pipeline as the agent's own tool calls, so what you fix in the UI is precisely what the model sees next session.

### 👆 Touch activation — CLAUDE.md semantics (v0.13)

Project memories carry sub-directory tags. A tag injects when the session's working directory sits inside it — **or the moment the session touches it**: one `read`/`edit`/`write`/`grep`/`glob`/`bash`/`pwsh` call into `frontend/src` activates `[frontend]` and `[frontend/src]` for the rest of the session. Activation is monotone and survives session resume — exactly like nested CLAUDE.md files, triggered by what you actually do, not just where you `cd`'d at launch.

Untouched areas are hinted, never silently hidden: `+3 more tagged to areas you haven't touched — memory_search surfaces them.`

### 🧠 Session-scoped — reads and writes agree

Each session's prompt carries ITS workspace's memories, and `memory_save` lands in that same workspace. Multi-session web hosts get zero cross-workspace bleed.

### 📉 Bounded by design

Root-level memories always inject; area memories load on work/touch; a 25-entry injection cap plus hard limits — 200 lines / 25 KB index, 500 memories per scope — keep the prompt flat no matter how much you remember.

### 🔒 Safety in the plumbing

Atomic writes (a crash never leaves half a file) · secrets refused on **every** write path, panel included · cross-origin + method gate on the panel API · traversal-proof ids · `$HOME`, drive roots and tmp dirs can never become a project scope (Windows-aware guards).

### 🪶 Zero dependencies

Nothing to provision, nothing to break. Lean hosts degrade gracefully — every optional host service is read defensively, tools keep working without them.

## Quick start

**Prerequisite**: the DSH CLI — `npm install -g @deepseek-ai/dsh`. From a source checkout, prefix commands with `pnpm`.

**1 · Install (one command)**

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add @fooxe/dsh-memory        # DSH CLI installed
pnpm dsh plugin --profile web add @fooxe/dsh-memory   # from a source checkout
```

`--profile` is **required** and goes **before** `add` — pick the profile you actually boot (`web` for the Web UI; see `~/.dsh/profiles/`). Manual `npm i -g @fooxe/dsh-memory` + `dsh web --patch ./overlay/dsh-memory.cordis.yml` also works, but `plugin add` is the recommended path.

**2 · Restart DSH — the step everyone misses**

Tools register **only at service startup**. Stop the service (Ctrl+C), start it again, then open a **new** chat.

**3 · Verify (30 seconds)**

Say *"Remember that I prefer pnpm over npm."* → a `memory_save` call appears. Open a **new** session and ask *"Which package manager do I prefer?"* → answered from the injected index. `~/.dsh/memory/MEMORY.md` now exists; inside a project, decisions land in `<project-root>/.dsh/memory/` — commit it and the whole team shares it.

### Troubleshooting (every row battle-tested on a real install)

| Symptom | Fix |
|---|---|
| `dsh: command not found` | Install the DSH CLI first — see Prerequisite |
| `required option '--profile <name>'` | It goes **before** the subcommand: `dsh plugin --profile web add ...` |
| pnpm `ERR_P..._STORE: Unexpected store location` | Your terminal pnpm differs from DSH's bundled one (11.7.0). Delete the profile dir (`~/.dsh/profiles/web`) and re-run `plugin add` — it rebuilds cleanly |
| Installed + restarted, still no memory tools | Check startup logs for `warning: ... did not activate`, and `dsh --profile web --dump-config \| grep fooxe` to confirm the tree entry; file an issue with the log if it persists |
| `ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS` after install | Harmless here (zero native deps); `pnpm approve-builds` in the profile dir clears it |
| `plugin add` installs an **old version** | Your default registry (a mirror) lags behind npmjs. Pin explicitly: `npx pnpm@11.7.0 add @fooxe/dsh-memory@latest --registry=https://registry.npmjs.org`, or add `@fooxe:registry=https://registry.npmjs.org` to `~/.npmrc` |

## Tools

| Tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `memory_save` | Save a durable memory; scope defaults to project inside a detected project root, user elsewhere |
| `memory_search` | Case-insensitive keyword search across both scopes (ids, titles, tags, content) |
| `memory_read` | Read one full memory — Claude Code's `project_memory_read` field contract (`content?`, `local_file?`, `size_bytes`, `updated_at`, `truncated`) |
| `memory_list` | Recent memories per scope, newest first |

Tool descriptions embed proactive-save guidance — preferences, decisions and key facts get saved without being asked; secrets never do.

**Write rules (ported from Claude Code / Gemini CLI practice):**
- **Strong-evidence gate** — before saving, the model asks *"will this still matter a month from now?"*; unsure → skip (noise costs more than gaps)
- **Dedupe-and-update** — same-topic saves update the memory in place instead of appending duplicates
- **Dated index lines** — every entry carries `YYYY-MM-DD`, so the model reasons fresh-vs-stale at injection time
- **Secret refusal** — credentials/tokens/passwords are refused out loud, on every write path

## When · what · which scope

**Save when**: a preference or correction is stated (corrections are the highest-value memories), a decision is made, a key number/ID appears, an error+fix closes. **Never**: secrets, transient state, anything directly readable from the repo, unconfirmed guesses.

**Which scope** — the one-line test: is this fact about *the person* or about *this project*?

| User scope `~/.dsh/memory` | Project scope `<project-root>/.dsh/memory` |
|---|---|
| Personal preferences (pnpm, Chinese comments) | Technical decisions (A over B, because C) |
| Working habits (test before commit) | Conventions (layout, naming, build commands) |
| Cross-project lessons | Key numbers / IDs (ports, servers, app IDs) |
| Communication style | Anything the team should share through the repo |

Still true in a different project? → user scope. Only true here? → project scope.

## How it works

**Two physically isolated stores** — user `~/.dsh/memory` and project `<project-root>/.dsh/memory` — that can never mix. The project root is auto-detected by a priority chain, clearest signal first:

1. `DSH_MEMORY_PROJECT_DIR` env override
2. An existing `.dsh/memory` marker above (supports nested sub-project scopes)
3. Any VCS root above: `.git` / `.svn` / `.hg`
4. The host workspace registry (DSH's official project registry)
5. The current directory itself — VCS-less projects get their own scope

**Storage layout**

```
~/.dsh/memory/                      <- user scope (personal, cross-project)
|-- MEMORY.md                       <- guarded index, newest first
|-- memories/20261004-181500-prefer-pnpm.md
<project-root>/.dsh/memory/         <- project scope (team-shared, commit it)
```

**Injection** happens at session start via `ctx.systemPrompt`: user memories always; project root-level memories always; path-tagged memories when the tag hits the session's working-directory chain **or a touched directory's chain** (see Touch activation above); untouched tags counted in the hint line; 25-entry cap on top of the scope-level guards.

## Verification

```sh
npm install && npm run build && npm test   # 64 tests, zero type errors
```

Unit + type compile against the shipped official types + runtime smoke (real `defineTool`, end-to-end save → search → read → list) + a real-cordis activation guard, with CI on Ubuntu **and** Windows.

dsh-memory happily coexists with DSH's official MCP memory options — pick whichever fits your workflow, or use both.

# 中文版

**给 DeepSeek Harness 装上跨会话持久记忆——Claude Code 的记忆模型：你的 agent 记得住、醒得来、项目之间不串味。纯文件、零依赖。**（[English](#english)）

## 这个插件做什么

> 你的 DSH agent 每次开会话都是"初次见面"。
> 装上 dsh-memory，它记得你。

```text
会话 1   你："记住——这个项目用 pnpm，不用 npm。"
         Agent：memory_save 已保存

会话 2   你："我们用什么包管理器？"
         Agent："pnpm——你昨天告诉我的。"   <- 从此不用重复解释
```

无服务端、无账号、无 embedding——只有纯 markdown 文件，删掉目录就是彻底遗忘。

## 亮点

### 🖥️ 可视化记忆管理器，不是一堆 markdown

打开 **Settings → Memory**：双域全部记忆一屏可搜、工作区树形展开（嵌套子项目自动发现）、子文件夹分组、护栏仪表实时可见（行数 / KB / 文件数）。**面板内直接**新增、改写、打标签、删除任意记忆——和 agent 工具调用走同一条带护栏管线，你在界面改的就是模型下次看到的。

### 👆 触碰激活——CLAUDE.md 语义（v0.13）

项目记忆带子目录标签。标签命中会话工作目录（含祖先链）时注入——**会话触碰它的那一刻也注入**：一次 `read`/`edit`/`write`/`grep`/`glob`/`bash`/`pwsh` 调用进了 `frontend/src`，`[frontend]` 和 `[frontend/src]` 立即激活并保持到会话结束。单调递增、会话恢复后仍在——和嵌套 CLAUDE.md 完全同理，由你实际做了什么触发，而不只是启动时 `cd` 在哪。

未触碰区域不静默隐藏，始终提示：`+3 more tagged to areas you haven't touched — memory_search surfaces them.`

### 🧠 会话级——读写同桶

每个会话的提示词携带**它自己工作区**的记忆，保存也落进同一个工作区——多会话 web 宿主零串味。

### 📉 天生防膨胀

根级记忆恒注入；区域记忆工作/触碰才加载；注入 25 条上限 + 硬护栏（每域 200 行 / 25KB 索引、500 条）——记得再多也不撑爆上下文。

### 🔒 管线内置安全

原子写入（崩溃不留半截文件）· **所有**写入路径拒存密钥（面板也算）· 面板 API 跨源 + method 双栅栏 · 防 id 路径穿越 · `$HOME`、盘符根、tmp 目录永不成为项目作用域（Windows 感知）。

### 🪶 零依赖

没有要部署的、没有会坏的。精简宿主优雅降级——可选宿主服务全部防御式读取，缺了工具照常工作。

## 快速开始

**前置**：先装 DSH 本体——`npm install -g @deepseek-ai/dsh`（源码检出则命令加 `pnpm` 前缀）。

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add @fooxe/dsh-memory        # 已装 DSH CLI
pnpm dsh plugin --profile web add @fooxe/dsh-memory   # 源码检出方式
```

`--profile` **必填**且放在 `add` 前面——填你实际启动的 profile（Web 界面就是 `web`；已有哪些看 `~/.dsh/profiles/`）。

装完**必须重启 DSH**（工具只在启动时注册），再开新会话说*"记住我喜欢 pnpm"*验证。`~/.dsh/memory/MEMORY.md` 随之出现；项目内决策落在 `<项目根>/.dsh/memory/`——提交版本库全组共享。

### 安装排障（每行来自真实安装实测）

| 症状 | 解法 |
|---|---|
| `dsh: command not found` | DSH 本体没装，看前置步骤 |
| `required option '--profile <name>'` | 参数放在子命令**前面**：`dsh plugin --profile web add ...` |
| pnpm `ERR_P..._STORE: Unexpected store location` | 终端 pnpm 与 DSH 自带（11.7.0）不一致——删掉整个 profile 目录（`~/.dsh/profiles/web`）重跑 `plugin add`，全新重建 |
| 装了也重启了还是没有记忆工具 | 看启动日志 `warning: ... did not activate`；跑 `dsh --profile web --dump-config \| grep fooxe` 确认在插件树里；仍在就把日志发 issue |
| `ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS` | 对本插件无害（零原生依赖）；profile 目录跑 `pnpm approve-builds` 清掉 |
| `plugin add` 装到**旧版本** | 默认源（镜像）滞后。显式官方源：`npx pnpm@11.7.0 add @fooxe/dsh-memory@latest --registry=https://registry.npmjs.org`；或 `~/.npmrc` 加 `@fooxe:registry=https://registry.npmjs.org` |

## 四个工具

| 工具 | 作用 |
|---|---|
| `memory_save` | 保存持久记忆；项目内默认存项目级，否则存用户级 |
| `memory_search` | 大小写不敏感关键词检索（id/标题/标签/正文，跨双域） |
| `memory_read` | 完整读取——字段与 Claude Code 官方 `project_memory_read` 一致（`content?`、`local_file?`、`size_bytes`、`updated_at`、`truncated`） |
| `memory_list` | 双域最近记忆列表（新→旧） |

工具描述内置主动保存指引——偏好、决策、关键数字不用吩咐就存，密钥永不存。

**写入规则（移植自 Claude Code / Gemini CLI 实践）：**
- **强证据门槛**——存前自问"一个月后还有用吗？"，不确定就跳过（噪音比缺口更贵）
- **去重更新**——同主题再存 → 原地更新（内容替换、时间戳刷新），不追加重复
- **日期索引**——每条带 YYYY-MM-DD，注入时模型可推理新旧
- **密钥拒存**——凭据/令牌/密码一律拒绝并明说，覆盖所有写入路径

## 何时记 · 记什么 · 记哪级

**何时记**：偏好/纠正出现（纠正是最高价值记忆）、决策诞生、关键数字/ID 出现、踩坑+解法闭环。**永不记**：密钥、临时状态、代码里直接能读到的、未证实的猜测。

**记哪级**——一句话判定：关于"这个人"还是"这个工程"？

| 记用户级 `~/.dsh/memory` | 记项目级 `<项目根>/.dsh/memory` |
|---|---|
| 个人偏好（我用 pnpm、注释用中文） | 技术决策（用 A 方案，因为 C） |
| 工作习惯（先跑测试再提交） | 项目约定（目录结构、命名、构建命令） |
| 跨项目经验（"这类库都有 X 坑"） | 关键数字/ID（端口、服务器、AppID） |
| 沟通风格 | 一切该随版本库共享给团队的 |

换个项目这条还成立？→ 用户级。只在这里成立？→ 项目级。

## 工作原理

**两个物理隔离的存储域**——用户级 `~/.dsh/memory` + 项目级 `<项目根>/.dsh/memory`——永不混淆。项目根按优先级链自动判定，越明确的信号越优先：

1. `DSH_MEMORY_PROJECT_DIR` 环境变量
2. 向上找已存在的 `.dsh/memory` 标记（支持嵌套子项目）
3. 向上找任意 VCS 根：`.git` / `.svn` / `.hg`
4. 宿主 workspace 注册表（DSH 官方项目注册表）
5. 当前目录兜底——无 VCS 项目也拥有自己的作用域

**存储布局**

```
~/.dsh/memory/                      <- 用户级（个人，跨项目）
|-- MEMORY.md                       <- 护栏索引，新→旧
|-- memories/20261004-181500-prefer-pnpm.md
<项目根>/.dsh/memory/               <- 项目级（团队共享，随版本库提交）
```

**注入**发生在会话启动时（`ctx.systemPrompt`）：user 域记忆恒注入；项目根级恒注入；带路径标签的按"命中工作目录链 **或 触碰目录链**"注入（见上方触碰激活）；未触碰的计数进提示行；注入另有 25 条上限叠在域级护栏之上。

## 验证

```sh
npm install && npm run build && npm test   # 64 项测试，0 类型错误
```

单元 + 对官方类型真实编译 + 运行时冒烟（真实 `defineTool`，save → search → read → list 端到端）+ 真实 cordis 激活守卫；CI 跑 Ubuntu **和** Windows。

与 DSH 官方 MCP 记忆方案完全共存——按工作流任选，或两者同用。MIT 协议，与 DeepSeek、Anthropic 无关联。

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-computer

A stateful Linux computer for the [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai) — a real Debian
box in a Docker container with a virtual display, Chromium, root-capable package installs, and a
persistent home directory.

This repository ships **two halves of one capability as a single package**:

| Half | What it is | How it lands |
|---|---|---|
| **The plugin** (`package.json`, `lib/`, `cordis.patch.yml`) | A DSH client+server plugin that puts an **Applications** menu in the Web GUI | `dsh.bundle.patch` — the profile lists the package as a bundle, and it appears in the Plugins panel with a toggle |
| **The skill** (`SKILL.md`, `bin/`, `image/`) | The agent-facing procedure that makes the capability *usable* | Discovered from a skill root as a loose `SKILL.md` |

The point of the single-package layout is that **one dependency delivers both**. A package installed
under a profile's `node_modules/` is simultaneously a bundle (for the plugin) and a valid skill root
(for the skill), so there is no separate copy step and no hand-appended config to drift out of sync.

## Install

```bash
# 1. Declare the dependency (pins a version)
cd /data/profiles/web
pnpm add github:BluePointDigital/dsh-computer#v0.1.4

# 2. Wire the rest: register the bundle, link the skill into the skill root,
#    build the box image if absent, then verify the whole stack.
bin/install.sh
```

`bin/install.sh` is idempotent and safe to re-run.

A restart is required after step 2: `dsh.profile.bundles` is the composition root, and
`patchReload: live` is **inert** on 0.2.0-rc.2 (see SKILL.md): every patch-layer change
needs a `dsh web` restart, and the bundle list needs one for a *different* reason --
bundles are resolved outside the Cordis module roots.

`SKILL.md` is what makes the agent aware the capability exists — and `bin/install.sh verify` is what
stops it from *believing* it has a computer when dockerd is missing.

## Requirements

- A reachable Docker daemon (nested dockerd is fine)
- `node` >= 20, `pnpm`
- For embedded desktop/apps: a browser that can reach the DSH GUI. No tailnet
  membership or per-app public hostname is required.

## Usage

```bash
bin/computer up            # create/start the box (idempotent)
bin/computer up --desktop  # ...and serve the display at http://<host>:<port>/vnc.html
bin/computer status        # container, display, ports, home size
bin/computer exec 'uname -a'
bin/computer sh            # shell inside
bin/computer apps          # the catalog the Applications menu renders
```

## Add applications (v0.2.0 candidate)

**My apps** is the installed/catalog app screen. **Add app** offers three paths:

1. Supported recipes: HTTP Echo, Nginx and the locally built Linux Desktop.
2. **Install something else…** opens a new DSH conversation with a draft setup
   request in the chosen workspace. The agent researches/prepares; you approve.
3. **Advanced** prepares a single-container image/entry/resources/data/env plan.

Every path uses one shared installer with a durable private registry, immutable
image review, explicit publisher-trust approval, progress, logs and owned rollback.
The agent never needs to edit node_modules or add a raw docker run command.
New apps publish no host ports. Uninstall keeps data volumes/images; reinstall
uses fresh volumes rather than silently adopting a previous install's data.

Preparation can download an image for review but creates/starts no container.
Same-origin app JavaScript shares the harness origin: only install trusted code.
This is an app installer, not a Portainer clone or a general Compose orchestrator.
See [installation contract](INSTALLATION.md) for limitations and recovery.

## Embedded applications

Applications launch **inside DSH**, under `/apps/web/<id>/`, including the noVNC
desktop. The plugin uses DSH's existing exact-path WebSocket route API; no
DeepSeek webapp patch or separate hostname per app is needed. Missing mounts or
capabilities produce an error rather than a tailnet-only fallback/new tab.

For a web app requiring sockets or literal API URL adaptation:

```yaml
web: 8092:3002
webSockets: /socket
webRewrite: /api/
```

Both fields are optional, space-separated lists. Socket paths are exact; rewrite
prefixes end in `/`. Prefer native application base-path support where available.
Legacy viewer-only catalogs remain supported; legacy direct-mode entries need to
switch to proxy. See [release notes](RELEASE-v0.1.9.md) for verification,
compatibility boundaries and the production release loop. This repository is the
source, not the running tag-pinned installation.

## Layout

```
package.json        the plugin manifest (name: dsh-applications) + dsh.bundle.patch
cordis.patch.yml    the bundle's mount row — the plugin's own declaration
lib/                plugin code: index.js (server), client.js (GUI), proxy.js
SKILL.md            the skill the agent reads
bin/computer        the CLI: up / exec / sh / status / apps / build
apps.yaml           the app catalog the menu renders (an allowlist, fail-closed)
bin/install.sh      idempotent wiring + verification
bin/switch-to-bundle.sh   migrate a profile from a hand-appended insert to a bundle
bin/test-switch.sh  round-trip test for the above, against a copy of the profile
image/              Dockerfile + box provisioning scripts
test/               plugin test suite
```

## Notes on the bundle form

A profile can mount this plugin two ways, and **exactly one must be present** — both at once
instantiates it twice:

- **bundle form (preferred)** — the package is listed in `dsh.profile.bundles`; its own
  `cordis.patch.yml` supplies the mount row. The Plugins panel lists it and gives it a toggle.
- **insert form (legacy)** — a hand-appended `- insert:` in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`.
  Applies live, but the panel cannot see it and it has no toggle.

`bin/switch-to-bundle.sh` migrates between them. It does both edits atomically, backs up first, and
refuses to leave the plugin mounted twice.

## Status / caveats

- **Verified:** the plugin mounts via the bundle form and appears in the Plugins panel; the box
  starts, serves its display, and runs commands; `bin/install.sh verify` passes.
- **How the skill reaches the agent:** skills are found by scanning skill *roots*, and a profile's
  `node_modules/` is not one — so a dependency install alone does not surface `SKILL.md`. The list of
  roots *is* configurable (`customSkillDirs`), and discovery accepts a loose `SKILL.md` at a root, so
  pointing it at this package would work — but that setting lives in the **agent preset** config
  (`preset-cordis`), not the profile, so it is not a profile-level toggle. `bin/install.sh` therefore
  links the package into the user skill root (`<dshHome>/skills/<skill-name>`), which every agent on
  the host sees. `watchFollowSymlinks` defaults to true, so the link is watched like a real directory.
- The image is **not** in this repository; build it from `image/Dockerfile`.

## License

MIT

# dsh-usage-tab 给 DSH Web 会话页签加一个 **「时间统计」** tab（排在 dsh-context 的「上下文」右边）， 把**本会话**的时间面貌画出来：挂钟跨度、活跃/空闲、每轮甘特、每小时分布、最慢的几轮。 **English:** Adds a **"Time Stats"** tab to DSH Web session tabs (placed to the right of **"Context"** from dsh-context) that charts the time profile of **the current session**: wall-clock span, active/idle split, a per-turn Gantt chart, an hourly distribution, and the slowest turns. > **P1 状态**：tab 界面 + 本会话真实数据。数据**全部**来自本会话已有的三条现成通道， > 不碰宿主日志、不扫盘、不读 `session_projcache`。跨会话 / 全历史是 **P2**。 > > **English:** **P1 status**: the tab UI plus real data for the current session. **All** the data comes from three channels the session already exposes; it does not touch host logs, scan the disk, or read `session_projcache`. Cross-session / full-history support is **P2**. > > **P1.1**：二级菜单（概览 / 日历 / 会话 / 设置）+ 三项偏好（空闲阈值 / 时区 / 数据范围）+ P1 口径止血。 > > **English:** **P1.1**: a sub-navigation menu (Overview / Calendar / Sessions / Settings), three preferences (idle threshold / time zone / data range), and stop-the-bleeding fixes for the P1 metric semantics. > > **P2 第一步**：宿主半边注册自己的会话投影单元 `usageDaily`（把**会话事件时间戳**按宿主本地时区 > 折成逐日活跃毫秒 + 总活跃/轮数/段数/最长段），**「日历」页读真数据** —— 走**会话列表行自带的 > 投影值**（`row.projectionValues.usageDaily`，零额外 I/O），跨会话求和成 今日/本周/本月 + > 近 12 周热力图 + 近 14 天柱状 + 段统计。**拿不到就保持空态**（值一律 `—`）。 > > **English:** **P2, step 1**: the host half registers its own session projection unit, `usageDaily` (folding **session event timestamps** into per-day active milliseconds in the host's local time zone, plus total active time / turn count / segment count / longest segment). The **Calendar page now reads real data** — taken from **the projection values carried by each session list row** (`row.projectionValues.usageDaily`, zero extra I/O) — summed across sessions into today / this week / this month totals, a 12-week heatmap, a 14-day bar chart, and segment statistics. **If none of it is available, the view stays empty** (every value shows `—`). > > **P2 第二步**：**冷会话回填** —— 启动 5 秒后（`BACKFILL_START_DELAY_MS`），对「从没打开过、 > 也没被写过投影缓存」的老会话逐条冷读日志、交给宿主 `sessionProjectionCache.coldSnapshot` > 补上 `usageDaily`。三条照跳的口径：**live 会话**（它自己会折）/ **缓存里已有该键的会话** / > **`header.cwd` 缺失的记录**（含子代理会话）。旧日志被源侧拒读（`SessionFormatUnsupported*`） > 时只记一条 `debug` + 一条计数 info，**绝不改写源文件**；单个失败不中断后续；卸载时 abort。 > 复验工具：`node tools/projcache-probe.mjs`（只读，回填前后各跑一次对比）。 > **实测复验（2026-10-13，重启后）**：`usageDaily` 覆盖率 **85.0% → 94.2%**， > 「只有本插件缺」**归零**；剩余那批全为「两键同缺」（源侧拒读，按红线接受并记录）。 > > **English:** **P2, step 2**: **cold-session backfill** — 5 seconds after startup (`BACKFILL_START_DELAY_MS`), old sessions that have **never been opened and never had a projection cached** are read back one by one from their cold logs and handed to the host's `sessionProjectionCache.coldSnapshot` to fill in `usageDaily`. Three cases are skipped by design: **live sessions** (they fold their own data) / **sessions that already have that key in the cache** / **records missing `header.cwd`** (including subagent sessions). When the source side refuses to read an old log (`SessionFormatUnsupported*`), the plugin records a single `debug` line plus one counter info line and **never rewrites the source file**; a single failure does not abort the rest, and uninstalling triggers an abort. Re-check tool: `node tools/projcache-probe.mjs` (read-only; run it before and after backfill and compare). **On-device re-check (2026-10-13, after a restart):** `usageDaily` coverage went from **85.0% to 94.2%**, and "missing only for this plugin" went to **zero**; the rest are all "both keys missing" (the batch the source side refuses to read, accepted and logged per the hard-line rule). > > **P2 第三步**：**「会话」页**（照一份「一页多视图 + 选项卡」的 UI 规范）—— > **A 默认**：按工作区分组的纵向表 + 行内比例条（回答"时间花在哪个项目上"）；**B**：逐日活动带 > （14 列 × 一行一会话，强度相对**全局最大单日**）；**C**：主从双栏（左栏清单、右栏选中会话的逐日条形 + 总量）。 > 数据全部来自**会话列表行自带的** `row.projectionValues.usageDaily`（零请求、零额外 I/O）。 > 🩸 **口径**：时长按所选时间窗（近 7 / 30 天 / 全部）逐日相加；**段数 / 轮数 / 最长段是宿主的全日志总量**， > 不随窗口变 —— 两类在卡面上分开写、绝不合成一个数。**拿不到任何一行 ⇒ 保持空态骨架（值一律 `—`）**。 > 三个工具条控件各管一摊：**视图**（A / B / C）· **时间窗**（近 7 / 30 天 / 全部，只管**时长怎么统计**）· > **显示范围**（7 / 14 / 30 天内 / 不限，只管**哪些会话还列出来** —— 按"最后活动日"算，**默认 14 天**）。 > 清单上限 `SESSION_LIST_LIMIT = 40`（**B / C 视图截断**；**A 视图列全部会话**、靠容器滚动 —— > 按全局 40 条截断会把排在 40 名之后的**整个工作区抹掉**），被截掉的数量写脚注； > 条长 / 档位 / 柱高的基准取**范围内全部会话**的最大值（筛选只改可见性、不改深浅的含义）。 > 五种"空"分开表述：显示范围挡光 / 工作区筛不中 / 窗口内无活跃 / 全零活跃 / 真的没有投影。 > ⚠️ **宿主半边（`lib/index.mjs`）与客户端半边（`lib/client.js`）的改动都必须重启桌面版 App 才生效** —— > 本机是 Electron 套壳，**没有「刷新页面」这个动作**。 > > **English:** **P2, step 3**: the **Sessions page** (following the "one page, multiple views plus a tab strip" pattern in a UI specification document) — **View A (default)**: a vertical table grouped by workspace with in-row proportion bars (answering "which project is the time going to"); **View B**: a daily-activity strip (14 columns by one row per session, intensity relative to the **globally busiest single day**); **View C**: a master-detail two-column layout (a list on the left, per-day bars plus totals for the selected session on the right). All data comes from **the `row.projectionValues.usageDaily` carried by the session list rows** (zero requests, zero extra I/O). 🩸 **Semantics**: durations are summed per day over the selected time window (last 7 / 30 days / all); **segment count / turn count / longest segment are the host's whole-log totals** and do not change with the window — the two kinds are written separately on the card and never blended into a single number. **If no row is available, the skeleton stays empty (every value `—`).** The three toolbar controls each own one thing: **View** (A / B / C) · **Time window** (last 7 / 30 days / all, controlling only **how durations are counted**) · **Display range** (within 7 / 14 / 30 days / unlimited, controlling only **which sessions are still listed**, computed from the "last active day", **default 14 days**; sessions untouched for too long are hidden by default). The list cap is `SESSION_LIST_LIMIT = 40` (**Views B / C truncate**; **View A lists every session** and relies on container scrolling — truncating globally at 40 would **wipe out entire workspaces** ranked past 40), and the number cut off is written in a footnote. The baselines for bar length / shading level / bar height are taken from the maximum across **all sessions in range** (filtering only changes visibility, not what the shading means). The five kinds of "empty" are described separately: cut off by the display range / filtered out by workspace / no activity inside the window / all-zero activity / genuinely no projection. ⚠️ **Changes to either the host half (`lib/index.mjs`) or the client half (`lib/client.js`) only take effect after restarting the desktop app** — this machine runs the Electron shell, so there is **no "refresh the page" action**. --- ## 一眼看懂 / At a Glance | 卡片 / Card | 画什么 / What it draws | 数据来自 / Data source | |---|---|---| | **本会话概览**

Most backfill cases are **asynchronous** (backfill runs inside `setTimeout` + `await`); they are registered through `testAsync` and awaited together after the synchronous cases finish. 另有两条结构/反事实脚本（期望：`OK=91 BAD=0` 与 `OK=121 BAD=0`）： **English:** There are also two structural / counterfactual scripts (expected: `OK=91 BAD=0` and `OK=121 BAD=0`): ```powershell node tools/struct-check-subnav.mjs # 结构自检：静态锚点 + 渲染 + 坏值注入（含 G15~G17 清洗闸 / inject） node tools/counterfactual-subnav.mjs # 反事实：拆掉修复点 ⇒ 真实 self-test / struct-check 必须变红（双驱动） ``` --- ## 安装 / Install **本机现状：已装（路 B，多个 profile —— 名字随机器而定）** —— `tools/install.mjs --apply` 做的事： ① 备份 profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml`；② 把源码（排除内部文档与产物目录）铺到 `~\.dsh\profiles\\vendor\dsh-usage-tab-src\`；③ 在 `profile\node_modules\` 建 Junction 指过去； ④ 往 profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml` 插一行 `- insert: { id: usage-tab, name: 'dsh-usage-tab' }`。 **English:** **Current state on this machine: installed (route B, several profiles — names vary by machine)** — what `tools/install.mjs --apply` does: (1) backs up the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`; (2) copies the source (excluding internal docs and artifact directories) to `~\.dsh\profiles\\vendor\dsh-usage-tab-src\`; (3) creates a junction in `profile\node_modules\` pointing there; (4) inserts the line `- insert: { id: usage-tab, name: 'dsh-usage-tab' }` into the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`. ⚠️ **2026-10-13 修正**：旧版把 profile 硬编码成 `web`（而日常实际跑的是 **desktop**）⇒ 改了 `lib/` 跑 `--apply` 只同步 web、**改完不生效且极难查**。现在默认自动枚举 `~\.dsh\profiles\*`、只处理 「已装过本插件」的那些（`--profile <名字>` 可显式指定单个）。 **English:** ⚠️ **Fixed on 2026-10-13**: an earlier version hard-coded the profile to `web` (while what actually runs day to day is **desktop**) ⇒ changes to `lib/` followed by `--apply` only synced web, and **the change silently failed to take effect and was extremely hard to track down**. It now auto-enumerates `~\.dsh\profiles\*` by default and only touches the ones where **this plugin is already installed** (`--profile ` can pin a single one explicitly). ```powershell node tools/install.mjs # 干跑，看清要动什么 node tools/install.mjs --apply # 真装 node tools/uninstall.mjs --apply --backup "<安装时的备份目录>" ``` - 🩸 **改了 `lib/` 就要重新 `--apply`**（vendor 是**副本**，不是软链）。 - **English:** 🩸 **After changing anything in `lib/`, run `--apply` again** (vendor is a **copy**, not a symlink). - 🩸 **改了 `lib/index.mjs` 必须重启桌面版 App**（bundle 列表在启动时读、模块已进 require cache）； `lib/client.js` 同样随重启加载（本机是 Electron 套壳，没有"刷新页面"这个动作）。 - **English:** 🩸 **After changing `lib/index.mjs` you must restart the desktop app** (the bundle list is read at startup and the module is already in the require cache); `lib/client.js` is likewise loaded on restart (this machine is the Electron shell, so there is no "refresh the page" action). - 🔍 **回填复验**：重启后跑 `node tools/projcache-probe.mjs --keys usageDaily,contextActivity`， 看那批老会话的「缺」是否归零；宿主日志对应一行是 `dsh-usage-tab: 冷会话回填完成 N 个会话的 usageDaily 投影`。 - **English:** 🔍 **Backfill re-check**: after restarting, run `node tools/projcache-probe.mjs --keys usageDaily,contextActivity` and see whether the "missing" count for that batch of old sessions has dropped to zero; the matching host log line starts with `dsh-usage-tab:` and reports the cold-session backfill result for N sessions. - 🩸 **绝不跑 `pnpm install`**（会重新解包 `file:vendor/*.tgz`、覆盖本机 vendor 的 0.1.7 补丁）。 - **English:** 🩸 **Never run `pnpm install`** (it unpacks `file:vendor/*.tgz` again and overwrites the local vendored 0.1.7 patch). 官方路（需重启，未采用）：`dependencies` 加 `"dsh-usage-tab": "link:<路径>"` + `dsh.profile.bundles` 加 `"dsh-usage-tab"`。`cordis.patch.yml` 里的 insert 行两种方式共用。 **English:** Official route (needs a restart, not adopted): add `"dsh-usage-tab": "link:"` to `dependencies` plus `"dsh-usage-tab"` to `dsh.profile.bundles`. The insert line in `cordis.patch.yml` is shared by both approaches. --- ## 权限与依赖 / Permissions & Dependencies **依赖**：**运行时零依赖** —— 不引入任何第三方包（宿主提供的 `@deepseek-ai/*` 走宿主自身）。 **网络**：**运行时与仓库内工具均不发起网络请求**（全源码内无 `fetch` / `XMLHttpRequest` / `http` / `net` 调用）。 **文件**：宿主半读**插件偏好**与**会话投影缓存**；冷会话回填时只**读**会话日志来补投影，**从不改写会话文件**。 ⚠️ 仓库里的**开发工具**（`tools/`）**会写文件**：反事实脚本在系统临时目录建副本，并把日志写到 `out/cf-logs/`（`out/` 已在 `.gitignore` 内）。 **命令 / 凭据**：**运行时**不执行外部命令、**不读取任何凭据**。 ⚠️ 仓库里的**开发工具**会用 `spawnSync` 起子进程（跑自测 / 结构检查）—— **那只在开发时用，不在插件运行时路径上**。 **会话数据**：只用本会话的**事件时间戳**做统计，**全部本机计算、不外传**。 ⚠️ 以上是**源码面**的保守自述：**"未发现"不等于"绝对不访问"** —— 请以实际源码为准。 本插件**非官方插件**，与 DeepSeek 官方无隶属关系。 **English:** **Dependencies**: **zero runtime dependencies** — no third-party packages (host-provided `@deepseek-ai/*` come from the host itself). **Network**: **neither the runtime nor the in-repo tools make network requests** (no `fetch` / `XMLHttpRequest` / `http` / `net` calls anywhere in the source). **Files**: the host half reads **plugin preferences** and the **session projection cache**; during cold-session backfill it only **reads** session logs to fill in projections and **never rewrites session files**. ⚠️ The **development tools** under `tools/` **do write files**: the counterfactual script builds a copy in the system temp directory and writes logs to `out/cf-logs/` (`out/` is covered by `.gitignore`). **Commands / credentials**: the **runtime** runs no external commands and **reads no credentials**. ⚠️ The **development tools** use `spawnSync` to launch child processes (running the self-test / struct check) — **that only happens in development, not on the plugin's runtime path**. **Session data**: only the current session's **event timestamps** are used, computed **entirely locally and never sent anywhere**. ⚠️ The above is a conservative statement about the **source surface**: "not found" does not mean "never accesses" — please refer to the actual source. This is **not an official plugin** and is not affiliated with DeepSeek. --- ## 许可 / License MIT **English:** Released under the MIT License.

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-idea

Idea domain for the [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) — an
independent, external Harness plugin (`@dsh-external/dsh-idea`, loader id `dsh-idea`).

An **Idea** is a long-term, user-owned possibility / hypothesis / direction / opportunity that
evolves over time. The V1 core loop:

```text
Conversation -> explicit Save Idea -> Idea v1 -> dormant/active
  -> explicit Related Ideas -> Continue Discussion -> explicit Save Again -> Idea v2
```

Every Idea operation is user-triggered. There is no automatic detection, background monitoring,
automatic resurfacing, or hidden prompt injection.

## T1 scope (current)

Host-only domain + persistence foundation. Implemented:

- typed Idea domain model (branded ids, aggregate invariants)
- schema-validated `idea` storage domain (`per-record` layout, one document per idea)
- `IdeaService` (`ctx.ideaService`): `create` / `get` / `list` / `archive` / `evolve`
- immutable linear version history (ordinals `1..N`, append-only)
- source-discussion snapshot persistence (bounded, user/assistant messages only)
- optimistic conflict protection for `evolve`/`archive` (`expectedCurrentVersionId`)
- focused tests, typecheck, build

Not implemented (later tasks): web UI, `💡 Idea` button, preview dialog, Typert Remote API,
LLM extraction, Related Ideas, Continue Discussion, session context capture, embeddings, PAH
integration, automatic hooks.

## Architecture

One Idea is **one canonical aggregate record**:

```text
domain: idea      table: ideas      key: ideaId      value: IdeaAggregate
```

A save (create or evolve) is one serialized single-record `put`/`update` on the domain's write
chain — durability before memory, no cross-table writes (the current Harness `storage-domain`
has no cross-table transactions). Version history is an immutable linear append; archived is
retrieval filtering, never deletion.

Domain schemas are zod and enforce the aggregate invariants at the durable read boundary;
plugin `Config` is schemastery per Harness convention (T1 declares none).

## Development

Requires a local DeepSeek Harness checkout (installed and built) — it is the authoritative
API baseline and provides the packages this plugin composes at runtime.

```bash
pnpm install
DSH_CHECKOUT=/path/to/deepseek-harness pnpm setup:dev   # junction node_modules to the checkout
pnpm verify        # typecheck + tests + build
```

On Windows (junctions are used, no admin rights needed):

```bash
set DSH_CHECKOUT=D:\Harness\deepseek-harness
pnpm setup:dev
pnpm verify
```

Re-run `pnpm setup:dev` after any `pnpm install`: installs refresh `node_modules` and the
checkout links must be reapplied so the whole graph shares one module instance per package.

## Installing into a Harness profile (future)

The package manifest is bundle-shaped (`dsh.bundle.patch` -> `./cordis.patch.yml`), so once T2+
wires the host surface:

```bash
pnpm dsh plugin --profile web add D:\Harness\harness-plugin\dsh-idea
```

then restart the profile. The bundle patch inserts the loader row naming this package; Cordis
waits for `storageDomain` and mounts `IdeaService`.

## License

MIT
