English  ·  简体中文

dsh-opencode-patch

OpenCode on DeepSeek Harness
Gateway origin headers · Session affinity · Free-tier tool fallback · Live dual-mode quota meter

Quick Start · What this fixes · Interface · Configuration · Troubleshooting · Changelog · Contributing

--- `dsh-opencode-patch` is a DeepSeek Harness host plugin that keeps **OpenCode Zen & Go** models working inside DSH. Connect `claude-sonnet-4-5`, `gpt-5.4`, `gemini-3.8-flash`, `deepseek-v4.1-flash`, `muse-spark-1.3-contributor-free`, `qwen3.8-flash` and the rest of the OpenCode catalog without network rejections, Cloudflare challenges, entitlement mismatches, or invisible limits. **The default state.** Point DSH at OpenCode with no plugin and the models do not work at all — not on one shape, on any of them: - **The request is not recognised as coming from a coding agent.** DSH sends its own `User-Agent`, and no `x-opencode-client`, `x-opencode-project` or `x-opencode-session` at all, so the gateway sees an anonymous SDK call and the traffic falls under the abuse rules the vendor documents for clients that do not identify themselves. **The free tier is a separate matter and this is not its cause**: with every one of those headers restored, a CLI `User-Agent`, a valid session id and the `read`/`bash` tool schemas the fallback injects, a Zen `-free` model still answers `403 FreeTierError` from outside OpenCode while a paid model on the same request answers `200`. So the plugin does not offer a Zen `-free` id, and the headers it restores are for the paid routes and the vendor's stated client rules. - **A turn without a session id is rejected or left unlinked.** Every turn has to carry a stable `ses_…`-shaped id, and DSH omits `sessionId` entirely for subagents, background evaluations and modes like **Auto Review**. - **Free-tier `/responses` bodies are refused without `read` and `bash` in `tools`**, and DSH deliberately does not send them. - **The catalog is thin.** A bare `/models` listing carries ids and little else, so the picker shows unnamed rows with no prices and no context windows. **What is left once those work is a different problem, and it is not about the account.** OpenCode serves its models on **four different API shapes**, while DSH picks a transport from the provider row — one route can speak one shape. So a model served on Responses, Messages or Mistral answers `500` the moment the basics are restored, which is why this plugin routes per **model** rather than per provider. **What this does.** It restores every missing protocol element at the network layer — **strictly for OpenCode routes** (`opencode` / `opencode-go` / `opencode-responses` / `opencode-anthropic` / `opencode-google`). All other traffic (DeepSeek, OpenAI, Anthropic, GitHub) passes through untouched. **What you get.** A picker listing the whole OpenCode catalog with real names, prices and context windows; every model sent to the endpoint it is actually served on; and a live meter for the quota or the spend — no configuration. **Three things it is built around.** 1. **Minimal intrusion.** Nothing is patched globally: requests are intercepted only for the routes this plugin claims, and every other provider — DeepSeek, OpenAI, Anthropic, GitHub — passes through byte-identical. The composer meter is one switch away from being gone, not one screen away from being tolerated. 2. **A native DSH plugin.** One `apply()`, a settings card bound to its own namespace, services declared through `ctx.inject`, slots filled the way the host fills its own, and copy in both bundled languages. No private hooks, no patched host code. 3. **OpenCode API compatibility.** The traits the gateways actually check are restored at the network layer — a `ses_…` id shaped exactly like the CLI's own, official origin headers, parent-session lineage, and the free-tier `read`/`bash` schema fallback. **Highlights** - 🔑 Deterministic `ses_<12hex><14base62>` session hashing with KV-cache affinity across turns, subagents and forks - 🌐 Gateway origin restoration — `User-Agent`, `x-opencode-client`, `x-opencode-project`, parent-session lineage - 🧰 Free-tier `read` + `bash` tool-schema fallback, so a free-tier body carries the tool definitions its endpoint requires — one cause of a `403` removed, and not the whole of it: the gateway's gate is not in the request, measured - 📇 models.dev-backed catalog with offline shims and background SWR refresh — names, context windows, prices - ⭕ Live dual-mode composer meter — Go quota ring (5-hour / weekly / monthly) or Zen pay-as-you-go pill, plus session spend and model rate - 🕵️ Strict credential isolation — Zen keys (`oc_sk_…`) never query the Go quota endpoint **Contents** 1. [Quick Start](#-quick-start) 2. [What This Fixes](#-what-this-fixes) 3. [Supported Models & Protocols](#-supported-models--multi-protocol-routing) 4. [The Interface](#-the-interface) 5. [Configuration Reference](#-configuration-reference) 6. [Troubleshooting](#-troubleshooting) 7. [Compatibility & Verification](#-compatibility--verification) 8. [Deep Dive](./docs/deep-dive.md) — the protocol internals, out of this README 9. [Attribution & License](#-attribution--license) --- ## 🚀 Quick Start **1. Install** into your DSH Web profile (Node 24+): ```sh cd ~/.dsh/profiles/web npm install dsh-opencode-patch ``` The package is `dsh-opencode-patch` under every name it is used by: the dependency you install, the bundle entry in your profile, and the row the host resolves. **2. Enable the bundle** — add the package to the profile's `dsh.profile.bundles` array: ```jsonc // ~/.dsh/profiles/web/package.json { "dependencies": { "dsh-opencode-patch": "^0.14.0", }, "dsh": { "profile": { "bundles": ["dsh-opencode-patch"], "patchReload": "live", }, }, } ``` **3. Add a credential** so the quota meter can resolve a key — store `OPENCODE_GO_API_KEY` (Go subscription, `sk-…`) and/or `OPENCODE_API_KEY` (Zen pay-as-you-go, `oc_sk_…`) in DSH Credentials or your environment. **4. Restart `dsh web`.** The host bundle is only imported at boot (`hmr root: []`), so a restart is what loads `lib/index.mjs`; client UI changes (`lib/client.js`) only need a browser refresh. Done — the **OpenCode Patch** card appears under _Settings → Plugins_, and the meter mounts in the composer dock as soon as an OpenCode model is active. --- ## 🔌 What This Fixes | Without the patch | With `dsh-opencode-patch` | | :-- | :-- | | Zen free models fail with `403 FreeTierError` | **Not offered.** The headers and tool fallbacks are restored for the paid routes, but they are not this error's cause — measured with all of them in place, a Zen `-free` id still answers `403` while a paid model answers `200`, so the plugin hides the free ids rather than pretending to fix them | | Only one API shape can be served per route — the rest answer `500` once the basics work | **Per-model routing** — each model dispatched to the endpoint its own SDK names, read from the catalog | | Session IDs rejected with `400 MissingSessionID` | **Deterministic `ses_…` session hashing** and affinity across turns | | Subagents lose conversation context | **Parent session tracking** (`x-opencode-parent-session-id`, `x-parent-session-id`) | | Auto Review calls fail with `TRANSPORT: Connection error` | **Fallback session turn capture** preserving turn state across eval calls | | Quotas and balances are invisible | **Live dual-mode composer meter** showing Go quota or Zen pay-as-you-go | | Zen keys cause `403 EntitlementError` on Go usage | **Strict credential isolation** keeping Zen keys away from the Go endpoint | | Projects share a single `"global"` telemetry bucket | **Dynamic workspace attribution** resolved from the active `session.header.cwd` | | Gateway `/models` returns a truncated, unnamed list | **models.dev enrichment** with display names, context windows and prices | --- ## 🧭 Supported Models & Multi-Protocol Routing **Both endpoints, and both credential shapes.** OpenCode's catalog defines an endpoint at two levels: a **provider default** — `https://opencode.ai/zen/v1` for Zen, `https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1` for Go — and a per-model **inference** endpoint that overrides it when the catalog sets one (the CLI reads `model.api.url`, falling back to the provider default). The plugin pins neither: it matches the `opencode.ai/zen` marker, so a model served from the default and a model served from its own endpoint are both patched. Those endpoints authenticate in **two ways**, because they speak three wire shapes: the OpenAI planes send `Authorization: Bearer `, the Anthropic plane sends `x-api-key: `. The plugin reads **both** — `Authorization` first, then `x-api-key` / `api-key` — so a credential is captured whichever plane carried it, and the Go quota read still finds a key. The gateway serves four protocol families, and **OpenAI alone is two of them**: Chat Completions and Responses are different wire formats, not two names for one thing. A model that needs Responses does not work on the completions endpoint, and the gateway does not fall back — it answers `500`. DSH speaks three of the four families itself. The fourth — Google Generative AI — is served by **this patch's own adapter**, registered on the host's `llm` service under the route `opencode-google`, so all four are routed. See the table below. ### 1. OpenCode Zen (`provider: opencode`) — pay-as-you-go & free tier - **Anthropic Messages** (`https://opencode.ai/zen/v1/messages`): `claude-sonnet-4-5`, `claude-opus-4-7`, `claude-haiku-4-5`, `qwen3.8-flash` - **OpenAI Responses** (`https://opencode.ai/zen/v1/responses`): `gpt-5.4`, `gpt-5.2`, `gpt-5.1-codex-max`, `muse-spark-1.3`, `space-bunny-free`, and the free-tier `muse-spark-1.3-contributor-free` - **OpenAI Chat Completions** (`https://opencode.ai/zen/v1/chat/completions`): `deepseek-v4.1-flash`, `kimi-k2.5`, `kimi-k3`, `minimax-m2.5`, `glm-5.2`, plus free-tier `nemotron-3-ultra-free`, `ling-3.0-flash-fin-free`, `mimo-v2.6-flash-free` - **Google Generative AI** (`https://opencode.ai/zen/v1/models/*:streamGenerateContent`), served by this patch's adapter as `opencode-google`: `gemini-3.8-flash`, `gemini-3.1-pro`, `gemini-3.5-flash-lite` ### 2. OpenCode Go (`provider: opencode-go`) — subscription quota - **OpenAI Chat Completions** (`https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/chat/completions`): `deepseek-v4-flash`, `deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp`, `deepseek-v4-pro`, `deepseek-v4.1-flash`, `glm-5.2`, `glm-5.3`, `glm-5.3-flash`, `hy3`, `hy4-preview`, `kimi-k2.6`, `kimi-k2.7-code`, `kimi-k3`, `longcat-2.0`, `longcat-2.5-preview-free`, `mimo-v2.5`, `mimo-v2.5-pro`, `mimo-v2.6-flash`, `mimo-v2.6-pro`, `qwen3.6-plus`, `qwen3.7-max`, `space-bunny`, `space-bunny-free`, `step-5-preview-free` - **OpenAI Responses** (`https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/responses`): `gpt-5.6-luna`, `gpt-6-luna`, `grok-4.5`, `grok-4.6`, `grok-4.7`, `muse-spark-1.2-contributor`, `muse-spark-1.3-contributor` - **Anthropic Messages** (`https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/messages`): `claude-haiku-5-5`, `minimax-m2.7`, `minimax-m3`, `qwen3.7-plus`, `qwen3.8-flash`, `qwen3.8-max` - Monitored by the live 3-window quota meter (5-hour rolling, weekly, monthly). The full set ships in the bundled catalog — see [Authoritative Model Catalogs](#7-authoritative-model-catalogs-dual-local-shims--real-time-swr-updates). ### 3. How a model's protocol is chosen — and why you configure nothing Zen's provider-level SDK is `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible`. models.dev names a **different** SDK per model only when that model needs one, so the presence of `provider.npm` is the signal — and it is what decides the wire protocol. Nothing is matched by hand: | models.dev `provider.npm` | models | protocol | served from | | :-- | --: | :-- | :-- | | _(absent)_ | 28 | OpenAI Chat Completions | the route you configured | | `@ai-sdk/openai` | 30 | OpenAI Responses | `opencode-responses` | | `@ai-sdk/anthropic` | 18 | Anthropic Messages | `opencode-anthropic` | | `@ai-sdk/google` | 8 | Google Generative AI | `opencode-google` | | `@ai-sdk/mistral` | 1 | _(a dialect this plugin does not serve)_ | **not offered** | Counts are the **85** active `opencode` models in `models.dev` as of 2026-10-14 — everything else the vendor lists is deprecated or retired, and the patch ships only what the gateway still serves. The same 85 are bundled offline in `src/catalog-data.ts`, so every one of them routes correctly before the first catalog refresh; regenerate that file with `pnpm run catalog:shim`. The patch **keeps those two routes out of both the model picker and _Settings → Models_**. Three properties hold today, and one does not yet: - **You keep choosing.** The picker shows exactly the models you listed, and each one is matched to the right protocol automatically. OpenCode serves models on three shapes — OpenAI Chat Completions (the default), OpenAI Responses, and Anthropic Messages — and a model that needs one of the other two is dispatched to the route that speaks it. No second route to declare by hand. - **You are never offered a model that cannot work.** Every one of the four families is reachable, so no model is dropped for want of a protocol: the `@ai-sdk/google` models are served through the patch's own adapter, and the three DSH already speaks are dispatched to the route that speaks them. That holds for models you list by hand as well — one the catalog does not describe is routed by the family its id names (`gemini-*` to the Generative AI path, `claude-*` to Messages), and if the route you put it on cannot serve that protocol it is not offered there at all, rather than answering `400 ModelProtocolUnsupported` when you pick it. - **One credential, from wherever you already have one.** A routed model authenticates with the key you configured, resolved through the credentials service and never re-asked for — and if a route names no key at all, a stored login's token answers instead, so signing in is enough. Your own configuration always wins: the order is the pool, then the route's own reference, then the login, and nothing is consulted before the thing you declared. **The route, if you would rather declare it yourself:** `opencode-responses` — and `opencode-anthropic`, once you use an Anthropic-plane model — can live in your profile's `llm-pi-ai` `providers` block, listing the models it serves. Declaring it is a choice, not a requirement: ```yaml opencode-responses: api: openai-responses baseURL: https://opencode.ai/zen/v1 headers: authorization: Bearer unused # swapped for your key by the fetch patch models: - id: muse-spark-1.3-contributor-free name: Muse Spark 1.3 Free contextWindow: 1048576 maxTokens: 131072 input: [text, image] ``` **The plugin registers that route for you**, so the block above is optional. `responses-provider.ts` mounts the host's own `llm-pi-ai` in-process, isolated from the authorization and settings seams and behind an `llm` facade that forwards only the adapter registration — so the route lands without duplicating the catalog directory, the settings namespace, or a single sign-in flow. This is verified against the real harness, not a stub: the route registers, the host's 41 catalog entries and 41 sign-in flows are untouched, and unloading withdraws the route again. The routes inherit **your** credential: each one names the same `apiKeyEnv` your `opencode` route already declares, so a custom key reference is never asked for twice. Routes your profile already declares are left alone — the plugin defers to your model list rather than overriding it. If your host has no loaded `llm-pi-ai` entry, the plugin registers nothing and says so in the log; declare the route in your profile in that case. ### 4. Execution modes covered | Mode | What the patch does | | :-- | :-- | | **Interactive multi-turn chat** | KV prompt-cache affinity via a stable per-session `ses_…` id | | **Subagents & forks** | Child and parent sessions both hashed; lineage carried in parent headers | | **Agent teams** | Shared-workspace attribution preserved across orchestration turns | | **Experimental Auto Review** | Background audit calls with an omitted `sessionId` still get a deterministic turn state, headers and tool fallback — **but they take their route from the session**, so a session selected on a Zen free-tier model fails with `403 FreeTierError` no matter what the patch restores. The free tier is not served from here; see the row above | --- ### 5. The catalog: what gets merged, and what wins The model list is assembled from four sources, each answering a different question: | Source | Answers | | :-- | :-- | | Bundled shim | what can be offered before any network call — cold start, offline | | models.dev | the canonical spec, price and display name | | The gateway's `/models` | what **this account** actually has | | Discovery decoration | what `discoverModels` should answer | Merging is **additive**: adapter rows are kept, canonical rows are appended when a model is missing, and a row is dropped only when the provider-scoped retirement list names it — a fact, not a guess. Display names and prices come from models.dev, because a gateway listing carries ids and little else. Two things follow that you will notice in use. **Cold start is never empty** — the bundled shim answers before the first refresh, so the picker has models immediately. And **a model models.dev has no row for still appears**, with `—` where its rate would be: never a guess, and never the previous model's name. Both generated files are checked in CI (`catalog:shim`, `limits:shim`); they exit non-zero when the vendor's data moved, which is the only way to notice models.dev changing under you. → Protocol routing, the merge and the UI in technical detail: [`docs/protocol-routing-and-merge.md`](./docs/protocol-routing-and-merge.md) · [中文](./docs/protocol-routing-and-merge.md) ## 🖥 The Interface Two surfaces, one reading. Both are pure views over the same Host data. | Surface | Where | What it shows | | :-- | :-- | :-- | | **Meter trigger** | composer dock, beside the model selector | Go: a ring plus the window's percent. Zen: the session spend, and no ring | | **Meter panel** | click the trigger | The windows, the monthly allowance, the session spend, the Zen credit, the action links | | **Settings card** | _Settings → Plugins → OpenCode Patch_ | Eight controls, plus a live Go usage summary above them | Hovering the trigger explains its own number; clicking it opens the panel. The sections below show each surface, and [docs/quota-meter.md](./docs/quota-meter.md) documents every state it can be in. ### Settings card — _Settings → Plugins → OpenCode Patch_ Eight controls in three sections — the decisions a user actually makes. Everything renders from the platform's own primitives (`Switch`, `Tag`, `Button`, host tokens), and every knob carries a hint plus a reset-to-default affordance. | Section | Control | Default | What it does | | :-- | :-- | :-: | :-- | | **Gateway Requests** | Inject User-Agent | `on` | Restores the official OpenCode CLI `User-Agent` so Cloudflare WAF checks pass | | **Gateway Requests** | Inject Origin Headers | `on` | Injects `x-opencode-client` (and the origin header set) on gateway traffic | | **Gateway Requests** | Attach Workspace Project | `on` | Tags `x-opencode-project` with the active folder name; off omits the header | | **Models & Free Tier** | Enrich Models from Models.dev | `on` | Merges canonical specs, display names, prices and active free models into listings **and** native DSH discovery | | **Models & Free Tier** | Inject Core Tools | `on` | Adds the `read` + `bash` schemas free-tier `/responses` bodies require | | **Quota Meter** | Enable Composer Usage Meter | `on` | Mounts the live meter in the composer dock — the Go quota ring, or the Zen session spend | | **Quota Meter** | Credential Source | `auto` | Which key wins when several are known: **Automatic** · **Live request first** · **Declared key first** | Override-style knobs (literal strings, markers, route lists) are deliberately **config-only** so a default fits every documented setup — see [Configuration Reference](#-configuration-reference). The composer panel also shows the **session's accumulated cost and the active model's per-million-token rate**, and there is no switch for it: it is part of the panel rather than an option, so it is on whenever the panel is. The card also carries a **live Go usage summary** above the controls — the same reading the composer meter shows, in the layout the vendor's own console uses: one row per window, with what is **left** held out on the right. ``` Go usage Healthy ● 5 hours 0% used · resets in 4h 58m 100% left ● Weekly 28% used · resets in 3d 2h 72% left ● Monthly 14% used · resets Nov 7, 8:55 AM 86% left Monthly allowance mimo-v2.6-pro · Go $60 · Plus $120 ⓘ ``` Above both sits the **sign-in row** — the plugin's own OpenCode account, when you want one: ``` OpenCode account Not signed in [ Sign in to OpenCode ] ``` Click it and the card shows a short code, a link to open, and that it is waiting. Approve in the browser and the row becomes the account's email. It is a device flow, so there is nothing to paste and no token ever reaches the page — the credential is written and read on the host, and the card only renders what it is told. **If you do not see this row after updating, the host process has not restarted.** The host bundle is read once at process start, so a browser reload keeps running the previous `lib/index.mjs`; stop and restart `dsh web`. The row is the quickest way to tell, because it is new in the same build as everything else. "Left" is a percentage, never a dollar figure: `/usage` publishes a percent per window and no balance at all, and the plan tier is not discoverable — so a dollar remainder would be a guess. The ⓘ states that. A quota that cannot be read says so and prints no numbers, rather than a row of zeroes that reads as a measurement. ### Composer dock meter The meter mounts next to DSH's native `ContextMeter` in `conversation.composer.dock`: Per-state behaviour — the trigger's three states, both panels, what every row answers, and the three different kinds of "no number" — is documented in [docs/quota-meter.md](./docs/quota-meter.md). ``` ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ Type a message... │ │ │ │ [+] Attach [DeepSeek V4.1 Flash ⌄] [⬆]│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ [ ⭕ 73% Context ] [ ⭕ 42% Go Quota ] ← when OpenCode Go is active [ ⭕ 73% Context ] [ ⭕ $0.00 ] ← when OpenCode Zen is active ``` #### Mode A — OpenCode Go (`opencode-go`) - **Adaptive ring**: a real-time SVG ring for the window that answers the question. A window that is **out** — rate-limited, or at its cap — is shown, widest first (monthly → weekly → 5-hour), because a monthly cap explains a refusal the 5-hour window does not. Otherwise it shows the **5-hour** window, which resets soonest and so is the one you can still act on. On a **free model** the ring renders hollow in the muted track colour — the plan's limit says nothing about a bill that cannot be charged, and red against `$0.00` would read as "you are out of money". - **Semantic colors**: green below 80% (`--dsw-alias-state-success-primary`), amber at ≥80% (`--dsw-alias-state-warn-primary`), red at the cap (`--dsw-alias-state-error-primary`). - **Click panel**: three window rows with live reset countdowns and a bar per window, a session-spend row naming the **currently selected** model, a Zen-overflow row, a rate-limited alert, and act-on-it links. Hovering the trigger shows a `Tooltip` listing **every** window (`5 hours 11% · Weekly 33% · Monthly 16%`), because the trigger can print only one of them and the next question is always "and the other two?". - **A model the catalog has no price for reads `—`, not `Free`.** The panel names whatever the picker has selected, even when models.dev has no entry for it yet (it syncs on a schedule), because showing the previous model's name is worse than showing no price. ``` ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ OpenCode Go [Go Plan]│ ├──────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ • 5 hours ███████░░░░░░░░░ 42% │ │ Resets 3h 12m │ │ • Weekly ███░░░░░░░░░░░░░ 18% │ │ Resets 5d 8h │ │ • Monthly █████████████░░░ 65% │ │ Resets 22d 4h │ ├──────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ Monthly allowance │ │ mimo-v2.6-flash Go $60 · Plus $120│ ├──────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ Session Spend │ │ deepseek-v4.1-flash · $0.15 / $0.6 per 1M │ │ $0.42 │ │ Available Zen Balance │ │ Ready for overflow Ready │ ├──────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ ⟳ Updated 08:30 Upgrade Console › │ └──────────────────────────────────────────────┘ ``` #### Mode B — OpenCode Zen (`opencode`) A Zen route renders no Go figure anywhere: there is no ring at all (a gauge with no measurement is decoration), the label is the spend rather than a percentage, a rate-limited **Go** plan does not paint the **Zen** trigger as an alert, and hovering carries the price (`Session Spend $0.00 · Pay-as-you-go`). A Go window is a fact about a plan this route never bills against, so it does not appear here. - **Zen trigger**: the spend as its label, and **no ring** — the ring is a gauge, and Zen has no window to measure (`$0.00` before anything has been priced, `$0.42` after). The figure is the only real number available — OpenCode exposes Zen balance through console server actions that require a browser session, so an API key cannot read it. - **Pay-as-you-go panel**: header with a `Pay-as-you-go` badge, the session-spend row (when the price switch is on), and one link — [OpenCode Console](https://opencode.ai/console), labelled **Top up**, because top-up is what a pay-as-you-go user wants from that page and it has no URL of its own. ``` ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ OpenCode Zen [Pay-as-you-go] │ ├───────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ Session Spend │ │ Space Bunny Free · Free $0.00│ ├───────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ ⟳ Updated 08:30 Top up › │ └───────────────────────────────────────────────┘ ``` **The monthly allowance, and why it is a total and not a balance.** The three windows are shares of a per-model monthly **dollar** allowance — the vendor's own words: _"Usage limits are defined as monthly dollar amounts… 5-hour — 20% of the monthly limit; weekly — 50%; and monthly — 100%."_ So the meter prints that allowance under the windows: for `mimo-v2.6-flash`, `Go $60 · Plus $120`. It is generated from the vendor's Go documentation (`pnpm run limits:shim`, checked on a schedule in CI) because the page states outright that _"usage limits may change"_ — a hand-typed table would be wrong within a release, and a stale dollar figure looks authoritative. It shows **both tiers** rather than one, because the plan is not discoverable: `/limits`, `/plan`, `/subscription`, `/account` and `/credits` all return 404, and `/models` carries no limit. Guessing a tier would misstate the money by 2–3x. It is deliberately **not** a remaining balance. `GET /zen/go/v

# dsh-wechat-media

**Personal WeChat for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (`dsh`)** — scan a QR
code once, then talk to your agent from WeChat: one DSH conversation per contact or group, and two-way
text, images, video, documents and archives. Several WeChat accounts can be paired side by side.

**给 DeepSeek Harness 的个人微信桥**：扫一次码，之后就能在微信里和 agent 对话 —— 每个联系人/群各自
一个独立会话，文字、图片、视频、文档、压缩包**双向**互通，支持**多个微信号同时在线**（小号 + 大号）。

---

## What it gives you / 它能做什么

| Capability | Detail |
|---|---|
| QR pairing | Cards in the Plugins panel. The login token is stored under `$DSH_HOME`, so **restarting dsh does not need a new scan**; re-pairing is one click. |
| One conversation per chat | Every WeChat contact (and group) gets its own DSH session with its own context, created or resumed automatically. |
| Text both ways | Your message becomes a turn; the answer is chunked back to WeChat. |
| Media both ways | Images, video, documents and archives. Inbound files are downloaded and decrypted to `$DSH_HOME/wechat-inbox/<date>/<chat>/`; the agent gets the path, so a text model can read images through `read_image`. Outbound files are uploaded and sent by the agent through its tools. |
| Multiple accounts | Pair a spare account and your main account; each keeps its own token, cursor and session map. |
| Persistence | Accounts, receive cursor, per-peer context tokens, chat→session routes, allowlist and preferences all live under `$DSH_HOME/dsh-wechat-media/`. |

## Requirements / 环境要求

- **dsh 0.2.0-rc.2 or newer** with the standard agent loop and tools (the shipped `dsh web` / desktop
  profiles qualify), Node.js >= 22 (Node 24 tested), Windows / macOS / Linux.
- **A WeChat account that can scan a QR code.** A spare account is strongly recommended: personal WeChat
  automation is against WeChat's terms of service and carries a ban risk, whichever library you use.
- Outbound access to `ilinkai.weixin.qq.com` and `novac2c.cdn.weixin.qq.com`.

## Install / 安装

```sh
# from GitHub
dsh plugin --profile web add github:wjh-ux/dsh-wechat-media

# or from a checkout
dsh plugin --profile web add link:/absolute/path/to/dsh-wechat-media
```

Restart `dsh`, then open **Plugins → `dsh-wechat-media`** and press **Add an account (QR code)**.

重启 dsh，然后在 **插件 → `dsh-wechat-media`** 点「**添加账号（扫码）**」。

## Pairing / 配对

1. The card shows a QR code (it polls its own status and refreshes an expired code automatically).
2. Scan it with WeChat on the phone, confirm on the phone.
3. If WeChat asks for digits, type them into the card and submit.
4. The account appears with a status dot: `monitoring` means the long poll is running.
5. **Add an account (QR code)** stays available at all times — scanning a *different* WeChat account
   adds it as another account, so a spare and your main account can run side by side. Scanning the account
   you already have simply refreshes its login. Each row also has **Pair again** and **Unpair**.
6. Opened the QR by mistake? Press **Cancel** — the attempt disappears immediately instead of waiting for
   the code to expire. (A QR lives five minutes; an attempt gives up after eight, and at most three QR codes
   are issued per attempt.)

The QR encodes the landing-page URL the platform hands out — scanning it is what completes the binding.
Each account is stored under its normalized `ilink_bot_id` (`b0f5860fdecb@im.bot` → `b0f5860fdecb-im-bot`),
with `0600` permissions on the files that hold a token; accounts, cursors and conversation routes are keyed
per account, so several can poll at the same time.

## Where inbound files go / 收件目录

By default inbound media is decrypted into `$DSH_HOME/wechat-inbox/<date>/<chat>/`. That directory is
configurable, and the change takes effect without a restart:

1. **From the card** - the field under *Inbound files are saved in* submits a plain GET form (a navigation, not a
   fetch), so it works even in browsers where the card's requests never reach the plugin.
2. **From the control panel** - `/dsh-wechat-media/panel` has the same field and a *restore default* button.
3. **With the system folder dialog** - *Browse… / 浏览…* (card and control panel) or
   `GET /dsh-wechat-media/pick-folder` opens Windows' own picker on the desktop and saves the choice. A browser
   cannot hand over an absolute path (a directory input only exposes relative names), which is why the dialog is
   opened by the host (`powershell -STA`) rather than in the page.
4. **From the plugin config** - `inboxDir: "D:\\wechat-files"` in the plugin options, used when no runtime
   preference is set.

The order is preference (card/panel) → config → `$DSH_HOME/wechat-inbox`. Only an absolute path is accepted: a
relative one is refused with a message instead of being resolved against the process working directory, because a
silently different directory is worse than the documented default. `GET /dsh-wechat-media/state` reports the
effective value as `inboxRoot`, with `inboxRootDefault` and `inboxRootConfig` for comparison.
## Using it / 使用

Just message the bot from WeChat. A few things the agent can do from inside the conversation:

- answer through the normal reply channel (the bridge relays its final text automatically);
- send **extra** messages or **files** with its tools:

| Tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `wechat_send_text` | An extra text message, or a message to a different chat (`to`), pre-empting the automatic relay for that turn. |
| `wechat_send_file` | Send a local file back to WeChat. Images (`.jpg/.png/.webp/.gif`) travel as pictures, videos (`.mp4/.mov`) as videos, everything else (pdf, docx, xlsx, zip, 7z, …) as a file attachment. |
| `wechat_status` | Which accounts are paired and which conversations exist. |

Every incoming message is prefixed with `[微信 <name> <wxid>]` so the agent can pass the right `to` when it
answers a specific chat. Group ids look like `12345678@chatroom`.

## Remote approval / 微信里远程审批

When a WeChat-driven session asks for approval — a tool call the permission preset wants confirmed — the prompt
goes to the same WeChat chat, not only to the GUI:

```
⚠️ 需要你批准一次操作（远程审批）
工具：pwsh
原因：write outside the workspace

回 1 = 批准一次 · 回 2 = 拒绝
```

Answer `1` / `y` / `同意` / `批准` / `/approve` to allow that one call, or `2` / `n` / `拒绝` / `/reject` to
refuse it. The answer is **consumed** — it never becomes a new turn. If nothing arrives within
`approvalTimeoutSec` (default 120 s), or the prompt cannot be delivered, or the turn is aborted, the request is
handed back to the GUI, so an approval is never silently dropped. Set `approval: "ignore"` in the plugin config
to keep approvals in the GUI only.

## Contact allowlist / 联系人白名单

Every chat that writes to the bot is remembered, and the card lists them under **Contacts & groups / 联系人 /
群**, with **Allow / Ignore / Clear** per row and an **Only accept allowlisted chats** switch.

- The switch is **off by default** — otherwise a freshly paired account would look broken to everyone who writes.
- With it on, only chats marked *Allow* reach the agent; *Ignore* and undecided chats are dropped and logged.
- A decision takes effect immediately (no restart) and is stored in `peers.json` beside the accounts.

## Diagnostics / 排障

- The host logs one line per inbound message with the envelope's identifying fields:
  `inbound group chat=… session_id=… group_id=… room=… from=… type=…` — for a group that settles which id the
  platform expects as the send target.
- `node scripts/probe-group-send.mjs "<chatId>"` sends a labelled test message to one chat, prints the
  platform's `ret` for each addressing variant, and then lists the chats the bridge already knows.
- `GET /dsh-wechat-media/state` (loopback only) returns accounts, monitors, preferences, peers and live
  pairing attempts.

## Where things live / 文件位置

```
$DSH_HOME/dsh-wechat-media/            accounts.json, prefs.json, routes.json, peers.json
$DSH_HOME/dsh-wechat-media/accounts/   <account>.json (token, 0600) · <account>.sync.json (cursor)
                                       <account>.context-tokens.json (proactive-send windows)
$DSH_HOME/wechat-inbox/<date>/<chat>/  inbound media, decrypted, with the real extension
$DSH_HOME/wechat-inbox/frames/         frame grabs and other working files the agent creates
```

## Delivery semantics / 发送语义

- The agent's final answer is relayed automatically, chunked at ~2000 characters with a short delay
  between parts. If the turn already used `wechat_send_text` or `wechat_send_file`, the relay stands down,
  so an answer is never delivered twice.
- Replies settle on **that turn's** `turn/end`, not on whole-agent idle: a session shared with the GUI never
  goes idle, which is the classic way a bridge "loses" replies it actually received.
- Messages are deduplicated per account by `message_id`, and the bot's own messages (`message_type: 2`) are
  ignored.

## Implementation notes / 实现要点

Everything here was learned against the live platform; each item broke something first.

1. **`qrcode_img_content` is a landing-page URL, not an image.** The QR has to be rendered locally from that
   URL — which is exactly what the official client encodes. This package vendors
   [`qrcode-generator`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/qrcode-generator) (MIT, © Kazuhiko Arase) to emit an SVG.
2. **The media key has two encodings.** Outbound `aes_key` is `base64(32-character hex text)` — base64 of the
   hex *string*, not of the 16 raw bytes. Inbound accepts both that and `base64(16 raw bytes)`, so a client
   must handle both.
3. **The upload is AES-128-ECB ciphertext in the body** (`Content-Type: application/octet-stream`), and the
   result is the **`x-encrypted-param` response header**. The reported `filesize` is the *padded ciphertext*
   size (`ceil((rawsize + 1) / 16) * 16`), while `file_item.len` is the plaintext size as a decimal string.
4. **A `getupdates` client-side timeout is normal control flow**, not a failure: the server holds the request
   for its full window. Only real errors back off. `-14` in `ret` or `errcode` means the token is stale:
   re-pair. `HTTP 403` means a second poller is using the same token — one consumer per token.
5. **`ctx.webServer` prefix routes must be registered without a trailing slash.** Its matcher tests
   `pathname.startsWith(prefix + "/")`, so `/x/` would look for a double slash and never match.
6. **Tool parameters must not carry `required: false`.** The harness rejects the schema and the whole plugin
   fails to load; an optional parameter simply omits the field.
7. **A `link:`-installed plugin cannot `import "@deepseek-ai/…"`.** Node resolves from the plugin's own
   directory, which has no such dependency; the Cordis loader can resolve it against the harness root
   (`ctx.loader.internal.import(name, baseUrl, {})`).
8. **A session created by a plugin needs `agentPresets.mount` *and* `meta.agentPreset`.** Without the mount
   the agent publishes against the empty global layer: no tools, no prompt, nothing it could act with.
9. **The plugin-panel card needs a client module that registers the slots itself** (`plugins.bundle.config`
   keyed by package name, `plugins.row.config` keyed `<package>#<row id>`), wrapped in
   `window.__ModuleLoader__.load({ id, factory })`. Exporting a schema is not enough, and a missing wrapper
   fails the web boot.

## Limitations / 已知限制

- **Group sending is unverified but well-founded.** Receiving from a group works today. Every reference
  implementation addresses a chat through `to_user_id` alone — the official client, the Go library
  (`daemon365/weixin-clawbot`, whose `Target` holds only `ToUserID` and whose `ChatType` is inbound metadata
  hardcoded to `direct`) and the Python port (`SiverKing/weixin-ClawBot-API`, which has no `chat_type` field at
  all). This package sends the same way. What is *not* confirmed against the platform is which inbound field
  carries a group's addressable id — `group_id` or `session_id`; the host logs
  `inbound group chat=… session_id=… group_id=… room=…` when a group first writes, which settles it, and if the
  answer is `session_id` the fix is one line in `describeEnvelope`.
- **Stickers and unknown item types are dropped, but visibly.** A message that carries neither text nor a
  downloadable file is counted (`counters.unusable` in `/dsh-wechat-media/state`) and logged with its item
  types instead of vanishing silently.
- **Voice is not bridged as audio.** WeChat's own transcript rides along as text when present; the `.silk`
  payload is downloaded but not transcoded.
- **Proactive sends need an open conversation window.** Without a stored context token for that peer the
  server answers `ret=-2`; write to the bot first and the window opens.
- **One poller per account token.** Two processes using the same token get `HTTP 403`.
- **No message history API** exists on this platform; only live messages are seen.
- Media is capped at 100 MiB inbound by default (`maxMediaMiB`).

## Security / 安全

- No secret is stored in this repository, and none is written into a cordis patch. The bot token lives in
  `$DSH_HOME/dsh-wechat-media/accounts/` (mode `0600` where the OS supports it).
- The plugin never puts the token in a URL. Traffic goes to the two WeChat hosts above and nowhere else.
- The card's HTTP routes refuse anything that does not arrive over loopback.
- **Use a spare WeChat account if you can.** Personal-account automation is at your own risk.

## Prior art / 相关工作

This is not the first WeChat bridge for dsh, and the protocol work stands on Tencent's own MIT-licensed
client. Credit where it is due:

- **`@tencent-weixin/openclaw-weixin`** (MIT, Tencent) — the authoritative implementation of the iLink bot
  protocol this package's `ilink.js` was ported from.
- **[`BiBoyang/dsh-im-bridge`](https://github.com/BiBoyang/dsh-im-bridge)** — turn/approval push, in-chat
  approval, persistent dedup.
- **[`Jesse-njx/dsh-chatnode-wechat`](https://github.com/Jesse-njx/dsh-chatnode-wechat)** — conversation-node
  routing and inbound image handling.
- **[`zhengjy01/dsh-wechat-clawbot`](https://github.com/zhengjy01/dsh-wechat-clawbot)** (and its upstream
  `lubaiUwU/DSH-WeChatClawBot`) — the floating-ball QR panel and the gateway split.

Compared with those, this package concentrates on **media**: the others move text (one of them images) and
none send video, documents or archives. Pick one bridge and stay with it — two of them polling the same bot
token will collide.

## License / 许可

MIT — see [LICENSE](./LICENSE). The vendored QR encoder and the ported protocol client keep their own
notices, listed in [THIRD-PARTY.md](./THIRD-PARTY.md).

WeChat and Weixin are trademarks of Tencent. This project is unofficial and is not affiliated with Tencent
or DeepSeek.

It persists iLink credentials and connects contacts to model sessions, media transfer and an optional native folder picker. No candidate code or lifecycle hooks were executed; runtime safety and compatibility are unproven.

# @wulongxi/dsh-skills-hub

**Skills Hub** is a [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH) plugin that adds a native, first-class panel to the web GUI for discovering, installing, and managing Agent Skills.

It ships three capabilities in one panel:

- **Market** — search online skill registries (default: [skillhub.cn](https://skillhub.cn), plus skills.sh and any public GitHub repository), preview a skill's full documentation, and read its file manifest before deciding to install.
- **My Skills** — browse every skill the runtime has loaded, grouped by source; enable or disable skills, edit their `SKILL.md`, or remove them (deletes go to `.trash`, never straight to disk loss).
- **Create** — write a new skill into the user-level or project-level skill root, with frontmatter handling handled for you.

The panel reads the official skill roots (`<project>/.dsh/skills`, `<project>/.agents/skills`, `~/.dsh/skills`, `~/.agents/skills`, plus any configured `customSkillDirs`) and merges the host's skill registry on top, so what the panel displays is exactly what the model receives.

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | Market search & preview: **available**. Skill installation: planned (see [Roadmap](#roadmap)). |
| Requires | DSH `>= 0.2.0-rc.2` |
| License | [BSD-3-Clause](LICENSE) |
| Languages | English, 简体中文 (follows the GUI language setting) |

---

## Installation

### From a local checkout (link install)

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add link:<path-to-this-repo>
```

Restart the DSH service. The sidebar then shows a **Skills Hub** entry; selecting it opens the panel in the center column.

### From npm (once published)

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add @wulongxi/dsh-skills-hub
```

## Usage

### Market tab

Type a query and press Enter. The source picker to the left of the search field selects which registry the search asks; the choice applies to the next search, so results always match the query that produced them.

- **skillhub.cn** (default) — a China-hosted skill store with 190,000+ skills, reachable directly with no network accelerator. The site explicitly invites agent integration: it publishes an agent-facing integration document (`install/skillhub.md`), allows crawlers in `robots.txt`, and its read path is unauthenticated. Rows carry Chinese descriptions, download counts, and icons.
- **skills.sh** — the Agent Skills registry's search endpoint. This source serves one page; the panel says so honestly instead of offering a load-more control that could only return empty.
- **GitHub repositories** — a repository can also be browsed directly: any `owner/repo` (a full URL or a `.git` suffix also works) is enumerated through the GitHub API, and every skill directory inside it becomes a row.

Long result lists load the next page automatically as you scroll, with an explicit "load more" button as the keyboard/click target. Selecting a skill's name opens a detail dialog rendered by the shell's own markdown renderer — the skill reads exactly as it does in a conversation — alongside its file list and total size.

### Installing from the market

The detail dialog carries the install action. A skill is installed **after** its body has been read, so the licence line and the file list sit on the same screen as the button. Installing asks twice: the target root (user `~/.dsh/skills`, shared by every project, or the current project's `.dsh/skills`), then a confirmation that states the licence situation at the moment of decision.

The install itself is engineered to fail cleanly:

- **Staged then renamed.** Files land in a staging directory beside the target and the directory is renamed into place only when every file arrived. A failed or cancelled install leaves the previous state of the disk untouched — no half-written skill the model could later load.
- **Collision is an error.** An existing skill with the same name is never silently replaced (the panel answers 409; updating an installed skill is M4's job).
- **Bounded.** Per-file 2 MB, 16 MB total, 200 files, and every manifest path is validated against a strict relative-path grammar before anything is written.
- **Provenance travels with the skill.** A `.skills-hub.json` record inside the installed directory names the market id, the source, the licence at install time and the timestamp — the anchor M4's update checks read back.

**Licences are stated, never laundered.** Every result row declares its licence: declared ones show it (MIT, GPL-3.0, …); undeclared ones show *No licence declared*. In a sampled catalogue more than half of the entries declare none, and that is a fact a user needs before deciding to copy a skill to disk.

### My Skills tab

Skills are grouped by provenance (project, user, plugin providers, runtime registration). A skill backed by a file can be enabled or disabled — the toggle rewrites `disable-model-invocation` in its frontmatter — edited, or deleted. Skills registered by plugins at runtime have no file on disk; the panel says so once, per group, instead of decorating every row, and their enable state is stored in the panel's own configuration.

### Preview

Every skill can be previewed, including bundled and runtime-registered ones that have no `SKILL.md` on disk — the host falls back to the runtime skill registry for those, and the dialog labels the source honestly ("from file" / "from skill registry"). Frontmatter fields are shown as a definition list above the body and are never mixed into the markdown, because a leading `---` fence is a thematic break in GFM and would mangle the YAML into headings and stray prose.

## Configuration

Plugin config (profile patch):

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | `boolean` | `true` | Master switch; `false` mounts no routes. |
| `githubProxies` | `string[]` | built-in chain | Accelerator prefixes for GitHub raw content, tried in order; include `""` to try direct first. |
| `customSkillDirs` | `string[]` | `[]` | Additional skill root directories to scan. |
| `dshHome` | `string` | `$DSH_HOME` or `~/.dsh` | Override for the user config root. |

## Security model

- **Every route sits behind the shared loopback fence** (socket address + `Host` header + browser same-origin markers). An unpaired LAN client receives `403 forbidden: loopback-only` before any skill file is touched. When `dsh-remote-web-ui` is loaded, a live paired-device cookie is an additional allow path; unpaired and revoked devices still receive 403.
- **A client-submitted `path` is only an identity claim.** Before touching any file, the host re-scans and requires the same skill name to resolve to that exact path. A project skill that disappeared can therefore never be redirected onto a same-named user skill, and the routes cannot be used to read or write an arbitrary path.
- **The browser never sends a URL.** Market requests carry only the opaque skill id the host issued; repositories, refs, directories and file paths are re-derived host-side, and the id grammar is validated segment by segment, so a path traversal is rejected before it can reach any fetch.
- **Remote fetching happens only in the host half**, behind the trust fence. The unauthenticated GitHub API allows 60 requests/hour, so only discovery (tree listing) touches it, cached for 30 minutes; file bodies come from `raw.githubusercontent.com` through an accelerator chain, which does not count against that budget. skillhub.cn is reached directly.
- **Registry icons are proxied, not linked.** Icon URLs are fetched host-side under an explicit policy (https only, allow-listed host, image content-type, 256 KB cap) and re-served as data URLs, so the browser never loads a third-party origin: no referrer leak, no tracking pixel per render.
- **Installs re-derive everything from the id.** The install route receives only the opaque skill id and the workspace the panel is showing; the file list comes from the skill's own detail manifest (never client-supplied), the target directory is derived host-side, and every manifest path is validated before it is joined onto the staging root. An install can therefore only write a skill directory under a skill root.
- Writes are bounded (64 KB bodies), symlinks refuse delete/update (both would escape their skill root), and deletes move files into `.trash` rather than removing them.

## Architecture

The package is a dual-half DSH plugin:

- **Host half** (`lib/index.js`, runs in the DSH server process) — serves the `/api/skills-hub/*` route family, owns all network access, file I/O, and the trust fence.
- **Client half** (`lib/client.js`, runs in the web GUI) — registers the sidebar entry and the center-column page through the shell's official slot seats (`sidebar.panellist` and the keyed `main` slot), so the shell owns the row box, active highlight and panel switching exactly as it does for its own Plugins and Schedule pages.

The client is built only on the host's frozen browser module table (`react`, `@deepseek-ai/cordis`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-*`); every control is the official shared primitive (`Button`, `Switch`, `Input`, `Menu`, `Modal`, `MarkdownText`, …) — nothing is hand-drawn. Registration failures are logged and degrade the panel; they never fail the GUI's boot.

## Development

```sh
pnpm install
pnpm typecheck        # tsc --noEmit
pnpm build            # tsc -b tsconfig.build.json && tsdown
```

Test suites (run with `node tests/<file>.mjs`):

| Suite | Scope |
| --- | --- |
| `m0-smoke.mjs` | Loads both bundles the way the host does; asserts the loader contract, injected-require usage and route registration. |
| `m1-host.mjs` | Drives the route family against a real temporary skill tree: scan grading, write-route identity checks, symlink protection, fence denials. |
| `market.mjs` | Market layer with fake transports, zero network: aggregation, dedup, id grammar (incl. path-escape attempts), source contracts, installer staging/path-safety/provenance. |
| `ui-structure.mjs` | UI guards: official-primitives-only, card anatomy, scroll height chain — each negative-controlled. |
| `theme-tokens.mjs` | Verifies every referenced CSS custom property exists in the shipped theme, because an undefined token makes `var()` silently drop the whole declaration. |
| `market-live*.mjs`, `icon-live.mjs`, `install-live.mjs`, `tools/scroll-selftest.mjs` | Manual, live-network / real-browser smoke tests; not part of the automated gate. |

## Project layout

```
src/
  index.ts                host entry: plugin contract, config, mount-once guard
  routes.ts               /api/skills-hub/* handlers
  access.ts, loopback.ts,
  pair-access.ts          trust fence (loopback + paired-device cookie)
  http.ts                 bounded body reader, JSON writer
  core/                   multi-root skill scan, frontmatter parse/rewrite,
                          provider toggle store
  market/                 source registry: fetch limits, TTL caches, accelerator
                          chain, skill-id codec, source adapters
  client/                 browser half: dictionaries, slot registrations, panel
tests/                    automated suites (see Development)
docs/                     design documents (Chinese)
```

## Roadmap

| Milestone | Scope | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| M0 | Plugin skeleton, sidebar entry, build pipeline | ✅ Shipped |
| M1 | Local management: browse / enable / edit / create / delete / preview | ✅ Shipped |
| M2 | Market: multi-source search, detail preview, paging, icons | ✅ Shipped |
| M3 | Installation engine: validation, size caps, atomic writes, provenance | ✅ Shipped |
| M4 | Lifecycle: provenance store, update checks, local-modification detection | Planned |
| M5 | Custom registry manifests, offline import, accelerator settings UI | Planned |

# DSH | dsh-plugin-cost-tracker | Real dollar cost per turn and per session, from pricing you configure

DSH's own `token-meter` plugin tracks tokens, but never dollars — its OpenRouter adapter discards the underlying cost field on purpose, and even if it didn't, custom-declared OpenRouter models aren't in the built-in pricing table anyway. This plugin closes that gap: it computes real cost from a small pricing table you maintain, and shows it right where you're already looking.

Cost is computed generically, keyed by `"provider/model"` (see `types.ts`'s `routeKey`) from DSH's own standard per-message usage accounting - it isn't tied to OpenRouter specifically. Route through DeepSeek's native API, OpenRouter, or any other provider DSH is configured with; add a pricing entry for whatever `provider/model` string you actually see logged and it's tracked the same way. The example below uses OpenRouter because that's this plugin's own development deployment - not a requirement.

## What it does

After every turn, it appends a collapsible notice showing:
- this turn's cost, broken down by prompt / completion / cache-read / cache-write tokens
- the exact provider/model that ran
- the running total for the whole session

![Cost notice, expanded](./screenshots/cost-tracker.png)

It also folds in subagent spend: any subagent/workflow delegation counts toward the root session's displayed total — only the top-level agent shows a notice, but nothing gets lost underneath it.

## How it integrates with DSH

Hooks `agent/turn-stopping` and appends the notice via `session.append('user/message', ..., { surfaceOp: 'append' })` — the same mechanism `packages/compaction/compaction-basic` uses in DSH itself. That's what makes it render as a normal collapsible "Context injection" row instead of forcing one more real LLM call just to deliver a passive notification (which is what `agent.inject()`/`steer()` would do).

## Configuration

Add an override for the bundle's `cost-tracker` row to your profile's `~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml`:

```yaml
- id: cost-tracker
  config:
    pricing:
      openrouter/z-ai/glm-5.3-flash:
        promptPerToken: 0.00000007
        completionPerToken: 0.00000025
        cacheReadPerToken: 0.000000007
      # ... one entry per "provider/model" you actually route to
```

Pricing isn't fetched automatically — it's a small table you keep in sync with https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models (or whatever provider you use), same drift risk you already accept for a hand-maintained model catalog.

## Install

Requires DeepSeek Harness **0.2.1-alpha.2 or newer** (see [DSH 0.2 update](#dsh-02-update)).

**From the app:** Plugins → install `@gz2016/dsh-plugin-cost-tracker`. Installing from the Plugins page also turns the bundle on.

**From the CLI:**

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add @gz2016/dsh-plugin-cost-tracker
```

`dsh plugin add` only runs `pnpm add`. Also add `"@gz2016/dsh-plugin-cost-tracker"` to `dsh.profile.bundles` in `~/.dsh/profiles/web/package.json`, then restart. DSH 0.2 loads a profile package only when it is selected as a bundle; it then applies this package's `cordis.patch.yml`.

## Known limitation

Any plugin that makes its own raw LLM call outside DSH's agent loop (bypassing its own request logging) won't be counted here — only requests the agent loop itself logs are visible to this plugin. This is about how the *call* is made (raw `ctx.llm.stream()` vs. the agent loop), not which provider it targets - a native DeepSeek or any other provider's calls are tracked the same as OpenRouter's, as long as they go through the normal agent loop.


## DSH 0.2 update

DeepSeek Harness 0.2 (0.2.1-alpha.2) changed several plugin APIs this package used, so the 0.1 release does not load on it: DSH disables it at startup because its peer versions are pinned to 0.1.1-rc.2. This release targets 0.2.1-alpha.2.

What changed:

- Notices use their own message source kind (`cost-tracker`). DSH 0.2 removed the shared `kind: 'plugin'` source; each producer now declares its own.
- Reads the session log through `session.snapshotEvents()`; `session.events` was removed.
- `peerDependencies` now name the 0.2.1-alpha.2 packages.
- Ships a `cordis.patch.yml` bundle layer (`dsh.bundle.patch`). DSH 0.2 only loads profile packages that are selected bundles, so install instructions changed (see [Install](#install)).

---

# DSH | dsh-plugin-idle-new-session | Auto-start a fresh session after a real gap

If you close the tab/PWA and come back hours later, DSH reopens whatever session you left open - which usually means picking up a stale, possibly unrelated conversation instead of a clean start. This plugin starts a brand-new session automatically when the app is opened (page load, or a backgrounded tab/PWA coming back to the foreground) 30+ minutes after the last time it was opened.

## How it works

Purely client-side and stateless on the host: it timestamps every "app opened" moment in `localStorage`, and if the gap since the last one is 30 minutes or more, it triggers a new session the same way clicking "New Session" would. A quick reopen (switching apps, a short break) does nothing - you land back exactly where you left off, same as today.

**"Client-side" here means it runs in the browser, on any device - desktop or mobile, not mobile-only.** "Host" is DSH's own backend/server process; "client" is the web page (Chrome on a laptop counts exactly the same as a phone browser or an installed PWA). Page load and tab/PWA-foreground are just the two moments a desktop browser tab and a mobile PWA each expose for "the app was just opened" - the same 30-minute-gap check applies identically either way.

## How it integrates with DSH

A pure client-side patch (`src/client.js`, no build step). The host half is a no-op - it exists only so DSH's own plugin-discovery scan finds and serves the client bundle.

## Install

Requires DeepSeek Harness **0.2.1-alpha.2 or newer** (see [DSH 0.2 update](#dsh-02-update)).

**From the app:** Plugins → install `@gz2016/dsh-plugin-idle-new-session`. Installing from the Plugins page also turns the bundle on.

**From the CLI:**

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add @gz2016/dsh-plugin-idle-new-session
```

`dsh plugin add` only runs `pnpm add`. Also add `"@gz2016/dsh-plugin-idle-new-session"` to `dsh.profile.bundles` in `~/.dsh/profiles/web/package.json`, then restart. DSH 0.2 loads a profile package only when it is selected as a bundle; it then applies this package's `cordis.patch.yml`.

No configuration - the 30-minute threshold is fixed today.


## DSH 0.2 update

DeepSeek Harness 0.2 (0.2.1-alpha.2) changed several plugin APIs this package used, so the 0.1 release does not load on it: DSH disables it at startup because its peer versions are pinned to 0.1.1-rc.2. This release targets 0.2.1-alpha.2.

What changed:

- Client `inject` list: the removed `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-runtime` is replaced by the packages that now provide each service (`slots` → `dsh-client-ui-renderer`, `workspaces` → `dsh-api-workspace-controller`).
- `peerDependencies` now name the 0.2.1-alpha.2 packages.
- Ships a `cordis.patch.yml` bundle layer (`dsh.bundle.patch`). DSH 0.2 only loads profile packages that are selected bundles, so install instructions changed (see [Install](#install)).

# DSH | dsh-plugin-image-picker | A real "attach image" button for the composer

DSH's own web client only supports adding an image by paste or drag-and-drop (v1 scope, per its own upstream design notes). That's a real gap on touch devices with no drag-and-drop, and on iOS specifically, where there's no clipboard-image paste at all - there was simply no way to attach a photo from a phone. This plugin adds a plain file-picker button to the composer toolbar that does.

## What it looks like

![Composer toolbar with the image-attach button](./screenshots/image-picker.png)

Tapping it opens the native file picker; the chosen image is fed through the exact same attachment path DSH's own paste/drop handling already uses (a synthetic `DataTransfer`/drop event), so there's no separate code path to trust - if paste-and-drop works today, this works the same way.

## How it integrates with DSH

A pure client-side patch (`src/client.js`, no build step): registers a composer toolbar seat and, on file selection, synthesizes the same drop event DSH's own composer already handles. No host-side plugin behavior.

## Install

Requires DeepSeek Harness **0.2.1-alpha.2 or newer** (see [DSH 0.2 update](#dsh-02-update)).

**From the app:** Plugins → install `@gz2016/dsh-plugin-image-picker`. Installing from the Plugins page also turns the bundle on.

**From the CLI:**

`dsh plugin add` only runs `pnpm add`. Also add `"@gz2016/dsh-plugin-image-picker"` to `dsh.profile.bundles` in `~/.dsh/profiles/web/package.json`, then restart. DSH 0.2 loads a profile package only when it is selected as a bundle; it then applies this package's `cordis.patch.yml`.

# DSH | dsh-plugin-model-icons | Per-provider brand icons on the composer's model button

Small composer polish: the model-select button shows a real brand icon for the active provider instead of plain text, and collapses to icon-only when the composer row gets narrow — the same responsive mechanism DSH's own built-in access-mode button already uses, applied consistently to the model button too.

## What it looks like

![Composer toolbar with brand icon on the model button](./screenshots/model-icons.png)

On a narrow composer row (a phone, or a resized desktop window), the trigger collapses to icon-only instead of pushing the row to wrap:

![Icon-only collapse on a narrow composer row](./screenshots/model-icons-mobile.png)

## Provider coverage

Detection works off the visible model name text (e.g. "GLM 5.3 Flash", "gpt-4o", "claude-3.5-sonnet") rather than an internal provider id — DSH's own model catalog wire type doesn't expose one to the client, so the name is the only signal available. Currently recognized out of the box: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google (Gemini), DeepSeek, Zhipu/GLM, xAI/Grok, Meta/Llama, Mistral, Qwen, Moonshot/Kimi, Cohere.

**A model from an unrecognized provider, or a newly released one that doesn't match an existing pattern yet, still works correctly** - it gets a plain generic icon (a small sparkle glyph) instead of a brand mark, never a blank space or a broken render. Nothing needs updating for the plugin to keep working as new models show up; only the brand-specific icon needs a new entry to appear (a name pattern + an SVG path, added to the `PROVIDERS` array in `src/client.js`) once a provider you care about isn't covered yet.

## How it integrates with DSH

A pure client-side patch (`src/client.js`, no build step) - it doesn't add any host-side behavior, just visual composer polish layered on top of DSH's existing model-select seat.

## Install

Requires DeepSeek Harness **0.2.1-alpha.2 or newer** (see [DSH 0.2 update](#dsh-02-update)).

**From the app:** Plugins → install `@gz2016/dsh-plugin-model-icons`. Installing from the Plugins page also turns the bundle on.

**From the CLI:**

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add @gz2016/dsh-plugin-model-icons
```

`dsh plugin add` only runs `pnpm add`. Also add `"@gz2016/dsh-plugin-model-icons"` to `dsh.profile.bundles` in `~/.dsh/profiles/web/package.json`, then restart. DSH 0.2 loads a profile package only when it is selected as a bundle; it then applies this package's `cordis.patch.yml`.

No configuration - it works out of the box for any provider already in your model catalog.


## DSH 0.2 update

DeepSeek Harness 0.2 (0.2.1-alpha.2) changed several plugin APIs this package used, so the 0.1 release does not load on it: DSH disables it at startup because its peer versions are pinned to 0.1.1-rc.2. This release targets 0.2.1-alpha.2.

What changed:

- Client `inject` list: dropped the removed `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-runtime`.
- `peerDependencies` now name the 0.2.1-alpha.2 packages.
- Ships a `cordis.patch.yml` bundle layer (`dsh.bundle.patch`). DSH 0.2 only loads profile packages that are selected bundles, so install instructions changed (see [Install](#install)).

---
*Unofficial project, independently developed and maintained by a community member. Not affiliated with or endorsed by DeepSeek.*
